01Chapter 1 · Hello Transformers

Hello Transformers — Transformer kya hai?

2017 me ek paper ne NLP ki duniya ko hamesha ke liye badal diya — usme Transformer naam ki ek nayi neural network architecture propose ki gayi thi. Isse pehle machine translation jaise kaam recurrent neural networks (RNNs) se hote the, lekin Transformer ne unhe translation quality aur training cost dono me peeche chhod diya. Aaj jo bhi bade language models aap dekhte ho, unki neev yahi architecture hai.

Transformer se pehle: RNN aur LSTM

Transformer se pehle RNN aur uska behtar version LSTM state of the art the. Inme ek feedback loop hota hai — network apni pehle wali state ki jaankari ko agle step me bhejta hai, isliye ye sequential data jaise text ke liye achhe the. Lekin inki ek badi kamzori thi: ye inherently sequential hote hain, matlab ek ke baad ek hi chalte hain, aur inki computation ko input sequence ke across parallelize nahi kiya ja sakta. Isse training slow hoti thi.

Encoder-Decoder framework aur uska bottleneck

Machine translation jaise tasks ke liye encoder-decoder ya sequence-to-sequence architecture use hoti thi. Encoder input sequence ko ek numerical representation me badalta hai, jise last hidden state kehte hain, aur decoder usse output sequence generate karta hai. Problem ye thi ki poori input sequence ka matlab ek hi fixed-size hidden state me compress karna padta tha — ye ek information bottleneck tha. Lambi sequences me shuruaat ki jaankari kho jaati thi.

Attention mechanism ne bottleneck ko toda

Iska hal attention mechanism tha: decoder ko encoder ke saare hidden states tak access milta hai, aur har decoding step par decoder har state ko alag-alag weight deta hai — jo words us waqt relevant hain, unpar zyada dhyaan. Isse model do bhashaon ke words ke beech sahi alignment seekh leta hai, chahe unka order alag ho. Lekin phir bhi encoder aur decoder recurrent the, isliye sequential problem bani rahi.

Self-attention: recurrence ko hata do

Transformer ne recurrence ko poori tarah hata diya aur sirf ek khaas tarah ke attention par bharosa kiya — self-attention. Isme attention ek hi layer ke saare states par kaam karta hai. Encoder aur decoder dono ke apne self-attention mechanisms hote hain, jinki outputs feed-forward neural networks ko milti hain. Ye architecture recurrent models se bahut tez train hota hai, aur isne NLP me haal ke breakthroughs ka raasta khola.

Transfer learning: akhri missing piece

Computer vision me transfer learning pehle se standard tha — ek bada model ImageNet jaise bade dataset par pretrain karo, phir use naye task par fine-tune karo, body aur head ko alag karke. NLP me ye saalon tak clear nahi tha ki pretraining kya ho. Phir 2017-2018 me naye approaches aaye: pehle ek framework jisne unsupervised pretraining se sentiment classification me strong performance dikhayi, phir ULMFiT, jiske teen steps the — pretraining (agle word ko predict karna, bina labeled data ke), domain adaptation (target corpus par language modeling), aur fine-tuning (classification layer ke saath). ULMFiT ne transformers ke liye missing piece de diya.

GPT aur BERT ne sab badal diya

2018 me do transformers aaye jinhone self-attention ko transfer learning se joda. GPT sirf Transformer ke decoder part ka use karta hai aur language modeling se pretrain hota hai — ise BookCorpus par train kiya gaya tha, jisme lagbhag 7,000 unpublished books the. BERT encoder part ka use karta hai aur masked language modeling se pretrain hota hai — isme randomly masked words ko predict karna hota hai, jaise "I looked at my [MASK] and saw that [MASK] was late." Dono ne NLP ke lagbhag har benchmark par naya record banaya. Uske baad se transformer models ki ek poori zoo ban gayi hai, aur alag-alag research labs ne apne models PyTorch ya TensorFlow me release kiye — jo hamesha ek doosre ke saath compatible nahi the.

Yaad rakho: Transformer = self-attention + transfer learning. Recurrence hatao, attention se har token ko poori sequence ka context do, bade corpus par pretrain karo, phir chhote labeled data par fine-tune karo — yahi formula aaj ke NLP ki neev hai.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Hello Transformers

01.1Chapter 1 · Hello Transformers

Hugging Face Ecosystem

Jab alag-alag labs apne transformer models alag-alag frameworks me release karne lage, to practitioner ke liye unhe apne kaam me laana mushkil ho gaya. Yahi gap bharne ke liye Hugging Face Transformers library aayi — 50 se zyada architectures ke liye ek unified API, aur uske aas-paas ek poora ecosystem ban gaya.

Transformers library kya karti hai

Ek naye model ko naye task par lagane me aam taur par chaar steps hote hain: model architecture ko code me implement karna, pretrained weights ko server se load karna, inputs ko preprocess karke model se guzarna aur task-specific postprocessing karna, aur dataloaders, loss functions aur optimizers ke saath training likhna. Har model aur har task ke liye ye custom logic chahiye hoti thi, aur research code ko adapt karne me aksar din lag jaate the. Transformers library ye sab standardize karti hai: ye teen bade deep learning frameworks — PyTorch, TensorFlow aur JAX — ko support karti hai, aur inke beech aasani se switch karne deti hai. Isme task-specific heads bhi hote hain, jisse text classification, named entity recognition aur question answering jaise tasks par fine-tune karna aasan ho jaata hai. Kitab ke hisaab se, isse ek practitioner ka kaam ek hafte se ghata kar ek dopahar ka ho gaya.

Ecosystem ke do hisse: libraries aur Hub

Hugging Face ecosystem ke mukhya taur par do hisse hain: libraries ka parivaar jo code deta hai, aur Hub jo pretrained model weights, datasets aur evaluation metrics ke scripts deta hai. Libraries me Transformers ke alawa teen aur important libraries hain.

Tokenizers

Har pipeline ke peeche ek tokenization step hota hai jo raw text ko tokens naam ki chhoti units me todta hai. Token words, words ke parts, ya sirf punctuation jaise characters bhi ho sakte hain. Transformer models tokens ki numerical representations par train hote hain, isliye ye step poore project ke liye bahut important hai. Tokenizers library kai tokenization strategies deti hai aur apne Rust backend ki wajah se text ko bahut tez tokenize karti hai. Ye normalization aur postprocessing jaise steps bhi sambhalti hai, aur tokenizer ko load karna bilkul waise hi hai jaise pretrained weights load karna.

Datasets

Datasets ko load karna, process karna aur store karna ek mushkil kaam ho sakta hai, khaas taur par jab dataset laptop ki RAM me fit na ho. Datasets library Hub par maujood hazaaron datasets ke liye ek standard interface deti hai, smart caching karti hai taaki preprocessing baar-baar na karni pade, aur memory mapping use karti hai jisse bade datasets bhi RAM ki limit se bach kar handle ho jaate hain. Ye Pandas aur NumPy ke saath bhi achhe se kaam karti hai. Classic NLP metrics ke alag-alag implementations me thode farq hote hain jo misleading results de sakte hain — Datasets metrics ke scripts de kar experiments ko zyada reproducible aur results ko zyada trustworthy banati hai.

Accelerate

Agar aapne kabhi apna training script PyTorch me likha hai, to aapko pata hoga ki laptop par chalne wale code ko organization ke cluster par chalana kitna sar-dard hota hai. Accelerate aapke normal training loops par ek abstraction layer lagata hai jo training infrastructure ke liye zaroori saara custom logic sambhal leta hai. Isse infrastructure badalna bahut aasan ho jaata hai.

Hugging Face Hub

Hub par 20,000 se zyada freely available models hain, jinhe task, framework aur dataset ke filters se dhoondha ja sakta hai. Model ko code me load karna literally ek line ka kaam hai, isliye kai models ke saath experiment karna aasan ho jaata hai. Hub par datasets aur metrics ke scripts bhi hote hain, aur model aur dataset cards hote hain jo batate hain ki model ya dataset ke andar kya hai, taaki aap informed decision le sako. Sabse cool feature: aap Hub par kisi bhi model ko task-specific interactive widget se seedha try kar sakte ho, bina code likhe.

Yaad rakho: Libraries (Transformers, Tokenizers, Datasets, Accelerate) code deti hain, Hub weights, data aur metrics deta hai. Dono mil kar modern ML workflow ka poora saaman dete hain — train karna, evaluate karna, share karna.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Hello Transformers
← Previous01 · Hello Transformers — Transformer kya hai?→ Next01.2 · Pipelines — Pehla Transformer Chalana
01.2Chapter 1 · Hello Transformers

Pipelines — Pehla Transformer Chalana

Transformers library ki sabse aasan entry point hai pipeline. Pipeline raw text ko fine-tuned model ki prediction me badalne ke saare steps ko abstract kar deta hai — aapko tokenizer, model loading ya postprocessing ki chinta nahi karni padti. Sirf kuch lines me aap NLP ke sabse common tasks kar sakte ho.

Text classification: sentiment analysis

Pipeline banane ke liye pipeline() function ko task ka naam dete hain. Pehli baar code chalane par model weights Hugging Face Hub se download hote hain, doosri baar cached version use hota hai. Default text-classification pipeline sentiment analysis ke liye design kiya gaya hai:

from transformers import pipeline
classifier = pipeline("text-classification")
outputs = classifier(text)

Har prediction ek Python dictionary hoti hai, jisme label aur score hote hain. Kitab ke example me ek gusse wale customer ki shikayat par model ne NEGATIVE label diya, score lagbhag 0.90 ke saath — matlab model bahut confident tha ki text ka sentiment negative hai. Sentiment analysis me pipeline sirf POSITIVE ya NEGATIVE me se ek label deta hai, kyunki doosre ko 1 minus score se nikala ja sakta hai. Ye pipeline multiclass aur multilabel classification bhi support karta hai.

Named entity recognition (NER)

Real-world objects jaise products, places aur people ko named entities kehte hain, aur text se unhe nikalne ko named entity recognition kehte hain. NER pipeline har entity ko ek category deta hai — jaise ORG (organization), LOC (location), PER (person) ya MISC (miscellaneous) — saath me confidence score aur text me uski start aur end position bhi:

ner_tagger = pipeline("ner", aggregation_strategy="simple")
outputs = ner_tagger(text)

aggregation_strategy="simple" se model ki predictions ke hisaab se words ko group kiya jaata hai — jaise do words se bani entity ko ek hi category milti hai. Scores batate hain ki model apni pehchan ke baare me kitna confident tha. Kabhi-kabhi model ek entity ko ek saath group karne me fail bhi ho jaata hai, aur uska confidence low hota hai — ye dekhna error analysis ka pehla kadam hai.

Question answering

Question answering me model ko ek passage (context) aur ek question diya jaata hai, aur model answer wala text span wapas karta hai. Kitab ke example me "What does the customer want?" poochne par model ne sahi answer span nikala, score lagbhag 0.63 ke saath, aur start aur end character indices bhi diye. Is khaas type ko extractive question answering kehte hain, kyunki answer seedha text se extract kiya jaata hai.

Summarization aur translation

Summarization ka goal lambi text ko chhota karke uske saare relevant facts bacha kar dena hai — ye pehle wale tasks se zyada mushkil hai kyunki isme coherent text generate karna padta hai:

summarizer = pipeline("summarization")
outputs = summarizer(text, max_length=45,
    clean_up_tokenization_spaces=True)

Keyword arguments jaise max_length se aap runtime par output ko tweak kar sakte ho. Translation bhi ek generation task hai — aap default model ko override karke apne kaam ke liye best model chun sakte ho, jaise English se German ke liye ek specific model. Hub par hazaaron language pairs ke liye models maujood hain.

Text generation

Text generation pipeline ek prompt ko aage badha kar text complete karta hai — jaise customer service reply ka autocomplete. Model prompt ke baad ka text generate karta hai, lekin uska output hamesha use karne layak nahi hota; kitab ke example me generated reply shikayat ko shant karne ke bajaye aur uljha deta hai. Ye ek yaad dilata hai ki generated text ko hamesha check karna chahiye.

Yaad rakho: Pipeline = task ka naam do, text do, prediction lo. Ye demo aur pehli koshish ke liye perfect hai, lekin apne data par fine-tune karna aage ke chapters ka kaam hai — saare models jo yahan use hue, wo pehle se fine-tuned public models the.

01.3Chapter 1 · Hello Transformers

Hugging Face Hub aur Model Sharing

Transfer learning hi transformers ki safalta ki sabse badi wajah hai — pretrained model ko dobara use karke naye task par lagaya ja sakta hai. Isliye pretrained models ko jaldi load karna aur unke saath experiment karna bahut zaroori hai, aur yahi kaam Hugging Face Hub karta hai.

Hub par kya milta hai

Hub par 20,000 se zyada freely available models hain. Models page par task, framework aur dataset ke filters hain, jinse aap jaldi promising candidates dhoondh sakte ho, aur phir unhe code me ek line se load kar sakte ho. Model weights ke alawa Hub par datasets aur metrics compute karne ke scripts bhi hain, jinse published results ko reproduce kiya ja sakta hai ya apne application ke liye extra data liya ja sakta hai. PyTorch aur TensorFlow ke apne hubs bhi hain, jo tab kaam aate hain jab koi model ya dataset Hugging Face Hub par na mile.

Model aur dataset cards

Hub model aur dataset cards bhi deta hai — ye documentation hoti hai jo batati hai ki model ya dataset ke andar kya hai, kis data par train hua hai, aur iski limitations kya hain. Card padh kar aap informed decision le sakte ho ki ye model aapke kaam ke liye sahi hai ya nahi. Har model ke saath ek inference widget bhi hota hai, jisse aap model ko seedha browser me try kar sakte ho, bina ek line code likhe.

Sharing ka culture

Hub ki taakat sharing me hai: koi bhi apna fine-tuned model upload kar sakta hai, aur doosre use bilkul waise hi download kar sakte hain jaise pretrained models ko. Aage ke chapters me aap khud apne fine-tuned models ko Hub par push karna seekhoge — push_to_hub se model public ho jaata hai, aur uske liye automatically ek inference endpoint bhi ban jaata hai jise HTTP requests se call kiya ja sakta hai.

Transformers ki asli chunautiyan

Media headlines se lag sakta hai ki transformers ki capabilities unlimited hain, lekin ye silver bullet nahi hain. Kitab paanch badi chunautiyan batati hai:

  • Language: NLP research me English ka domination hai. Doosri bhashaon ke liye models hain, lekin rare ya low-resource languages ke liye pretrained models dhoondhna mushkil hai. Chapter 4 me multilingual transformers aur zero-shot cross-lingual transfer isi ka hal dikhate hain.
  • Data availability: Transfer learning se labeled data ki zaroorat bahut kam ho jaati hai, phir bhi ek insaan ko task seekhne ke liye jitna data chahiye, usse zyada chahiye hota hai. Bahut kam ya zero labeled data wale scenarios Chapter 9 ka topic hain.
  • Long documents: Self-attention paragraph-lambi texts par bahut achha kaam karta hai, lekin poore documents jaise lambe texts par bahut expensive ho jaata hai. Iske hal Chapter 11 me hain.
  • Opacity: Doosre deep learning models ki tarah transformers bhi kaafi opaque hain — ye samajhna mushkil ya namumkin hai ki model ne ek prediction "kyun" ki. Ye khaas taur par mushkil hai jab models critical decisions ke liye deploy hote hain. Chapters 2 aur 4 me model ki galtiyon ko probe karne ke tareeke hain.
  • Bias: Transformer models zyadatar internet ke text data par pretrain hote hain, isliye data me maujood saare biases models me bhi aa jaate hain. Ye ensure karna ki ye biases nuksaan na pahunchayein, ek mushkil kaam hai — is par Chapter 10 me detail me baat hai.
Yaad rakho: Hub sirf model download karne ki jagah nahi hai — ye sharing, documentation aur testing ka poora system hai. Aur transformers powerful hain, lekin unki limits (language, data, lambe documents, opacity, bias) ko jaanna utna hi zaroori hai jitna unki taakat ko.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Hello Transformers

02Chapter 2 · Text Classification

Text Classification — Sentiment Analysis

Text classification NLP ke sabse common tasks me se ek hai — customer feedback ko categories me tag karna, support tickets ko unki bhasha ke hisaab se route karna, ya email ka spam filter, ye sab text classification hi hai. Is chapter me hum ek aisa system banayenge jo tweets me logon ke emotions pehchan sake, aur is bahane poora training workflow seekhenge.

Task: emotion detection

Sentiment analysis text ki polarity pehchanta hai — positive ya negative. Humara task isse ek kadam aage hai: tweets ko chhe basic emotions me classify karna — anger, disgust, fear, joy, sadness aur surprise. Aam sentiment datasets me sirf positive/negative hota hai, lekin ye dataset emotions ki detail deta hai, isliye ye zyada interesting aur zyada mushkil bhi hai.

Model: DistilBERT

Is task ke liye hum BERT ka ek variant use karenge jise DistilBERT kehte hain. Iska sabse bada fayda ye hai ki ye BERT ke barabar performance deta hai, lekin bahut chhota aur efficient hai — isse hum kuch hi minutes me ek classifier train kar sakte hain. Agar aapko bada BERT model train karna ho, to sirf pretrained model ka checkpoint badalna hota hai. Checkpoint ka matlab hai weights ka wo set jo ek transformer architecture me load kiya jaata hai.

Teen core libraries, ek workflow

Ye humari pehli mulaqat hogi Hugging Face ecosystem ki teen core libraries se — Datasets, Tokenizers aur Transformers. Inka workflow seedha hai: Datasets se raw text load karo, Tokenizers se text ko tokens me badlo, aur Transformers se model ko fine-tune karke naye tweets par inference ke liye use karo. Aage ke sections me hum is workflow ka har step detail me dekhenge — data load karna, tokenize karna, Trainer API se fine-tune karna, aur evaluation aur error analysis karna.

Do tareeke: feature extraction vs fine-tuning

Classifier train karne ke do tareeke hain. Feature extraction me pretrained model ke weights ko freeze kar dete hain aur uske hidden states ko features ki tarah use karke unpar ek chhota classifier train karte hain — ye tez hai aur GPU ke bina bhi ho sakta hai, kyunki hidden states sirf ek baar compute karne hote hain. Fine-tuning me poora model end-to-end train hota hai, jisme pretrained model ke parameters bhi update hote hain — ye behtar performance deta hai, lekin iske liye zyada compute chahiye hota hai. Is chapter me hum dono try karenge aur unke trade-offs ko compare karenge.

Yaad rakho: Text classification sirf positive/negative nahi hai — koi bhi fixed labels ho sakte hain, jaise chhe emotions. DistilBERT chhota aur tez hai, isliye seekhne ke liye perfect hai, aur checkpoint badal kar aap kabhi bhi bade model par switch kar sakte ho.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Text Classification

02.1Chapter 2 · Text Classification

Datasets — IMDB Data Load Karna

Koi bhi model train karne se pehle data ko samajhna zaroori hai. Ek mashhoor blog post me kaha gaya hai ki data ke saath "one" ho jaana great models train karne ka essential step hai. Is section me hum emotion dataset ko load karenge, inspect karenge, aur uski khaamiyan dhoondhenge.

Dataset load karna

Hub par maujood datasets ko list_datasets() se dekha ja sakta hai — kitab likhte waqt Hub par 1,753 datasets the. Emotion dataset ko load_dataset("emotion") se load karte hain, aur result ek DatasetDict hota hai — ek Python dictionary jaisa object jisme har key ek split hai:

from datasets import load_dataset
emotions = load_dataset("emotion")

Train split me 16,000 examples, validation me 2,000 aur test me 2,000 hain. Har example me do columns hain: text (tweet) aur label (emotion ka integer). Dataset ek ordinary Python list jaisa behave karta hai — len(train_ds) se length, train_ds[0] se pehla example, aur slice se kai rows ek saath mil jaati hain.

Features aur ClassLabel

Datasets Apache Arrow par based hai, jo ek typed columnar format hai aur native Python se zyada memory-efficient hai. train_ds.features se pata chalta hai ki text column string type ka hai, aur label ek khaas ClassLabel object hai jisme class names aur unki integer mapping hoti hai — sadness 0, joy 1, love 2, anger 3, fear 4, surprise 5. int2str() method se integer labels ko wapas names me badla ja sakta hai.

Dataset Hub par na ho to?

Aksar aapka data laptop ya organization ke server par hoga. load_dataset() local aur remote datasets bhi load kar sakta hai — format ke hisaab se loading script badalti hai: CSV ke liye "csv", text ke liye "text", JSON ke liye "json", saath me data_files argument me file ka path ya URL. Jaise emotion dataset ki source files ek file-hosting link par hain, to unhe seedha URL se bhi load kiya ja sakta hai — load_dataset("csv", data_files=dataset_url, sep=";", names=["text", "label"]). Separator aur column names bhi specify kiye ja sakte hain.

DataFrame me badalna

Visualization ke liye Dataset ko Pandas DataFrame me badalna convenient hota hai. emotions.set_format(type="pandas") se output format badal jaata hai — underlying Arrow format wahi rehta hai, aur baad me format wapas bhi badla ja sakta hai. Phir int2str() se ek label_name column banaya ja sakta hai jisme labels ke naam hon.

Class distribution dekhna

Text classification me hamesha classes ka distribution check karna chahiye. Yahan dataset heavily imbalanced hai: joy aur sadness bahut frequent hain, jabki love aur surprise lagbhag 5-10 guna rare hain. Imbalance se nipatne ke tareeke hain — minority class ko randomly oversample karna, majority class ko undersample karna, ya underrepresented classes ke liye aur labeled data jama karna. Is chapter me hum raw, unbalanced frequencies ke saath hi kaam karenge. Ek chetavni: sampling methods ko train/test split banane se pehle apply mat karo, warna splits ke beech leakage ho jayega.

Tweets kitne lambe hain?

Transformer models ki ek maximum input sequence length hoti hai jise maximum context size kehte hain. DistilBERT ke liye ye 512 tokens hai, jo kuch paragraphs ke barabar hai. Har emotion ke liye tweets aam taur par lagbhag 15 words ke hote hain, aur sabse lambe tweets bhi 512 se bahut neeche hain — isliye truncation se performance loss hone ka khatra nahi hai. Jo texts context size se lambe hote hain, unhe truncate karna padta hai, aur agar truncated hisse me zaroori jaankari ho to performance gir sakti hai.

Yaad rakho: Data ko load karne ke baad pehle use dekho — splits, class balance, text length. Imbalanced data aur lambi texts, dono training aur evaluation ko affect karte hain, isliye inhe model banane se pehle jaan lena chahiye.

    for split in ds:
        panx_ch[lang][split] = (
            ds[split]
            .shuffle(seed=0)
            .select(range(int(frac * ds[split].num_rows))))

02.2Chapter 2 · Text Classification

Tokenizer — Text ko Tokens me Badalna

DistilBERT jaise transformer models raw strings ko input ke taur par nahi le sakte — pehle text ko tokenize karke numerical vectors me badalna padta hai. Tokenization wo step hai jo string ko model ke atomic units me todta hai. Is section me hum teen tokenization strategies dekhenge aur DistilBERT ke tokenizer ko action me dekhenge.

Character tokenization

Sabse simple scheme hai har character ko alag se model ko dena. Phir har unique character ko ek unique integer se map karte hain — ise numericalization kehte hain. In integers ko input_ids kehte hain. Akhri step me input_ids ko one-hot vectors me badla jaata hai — har token ke liye ek vector jisme sirf ek entry 1 hoti hai. One-hot isliye zaroori hai kyunki integer IDs me ek fictitious ordering ban jaati hai — IDs ko jodna ya ghataana bekaar hai, kyunki result ek aur random token ka ID ban jaata hai. Character tokenization se misspellings aur rare words handle ho jaate hain, lekin words ko data se seekhne me bahut compute aur data lagta hai, isliye ye practice me rarely use hoti hai.

Word tokenization

Words se shuru karne se model ko characters se words seekhne ka step skip karne ko milta hai. Simple word tokenizer whitespace par split karta hai — text.split(). Lekin punctuation account nahi hoti aur declinations ya misspellings ki wajah se vocabulary millions me pahunch sakti hai. Itni badi vocabulary ek problem hai kyunki neural network ke pehle layer ki weight matrix bahut badi ho jaati hai — 1 million unique words ko 1,000-dimensional vectors me compress karne me hi 1 billion weights lag jaate hain, jo sabse bade GPT-2 model ke lagbhag 1.5 billion parameters ke barabar hai. Aam hal hai vocabulary ko limit karna — jaise 100,000 sabse common words rakhna — aur baaki ko ek shared UNK token se map karna. Lekin isse UNK wale words ki jaankari kho jaati hai.

Subword tokenization: behtareen compromise

Subword tokenization character aur word tokenization ke beech ka compromise hai: rare words ko chhoti units me todo taaki complex words aur misspellings handle ho sakein, aur frequent words ko unique entities ki tarah rakho taaki input length manageable rahe. BERT aur DistilBERT WordPiece use karte hain.

DistilBERT tokenizer action me

AutoTokenizer class se pretrained model ka tokenizer load hota hai — AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("distilbert-base-uncased"). "Tokenizing text is a core task of NLP." ko encode karne par hume input_ids aur attention_mask milte hain. Tokens me teen cheezein dhyaan dene layak hain: shuruaat aur end me khaas [CLS] aur [SEP] tokens add hote hain, saare tokens lowercase ho jaate hain (is checkpoint ki khaasiyat), aur "tokenizing" aur "NLP" do tokens me toot jaate hain — "token" + "##izing" aur "nl" + "##p". ## prefix ka matlab hai ki pehle wali string me whitespace nahi hai; string me wapas badalte waqt inhe pehle token se merge karna hota hai. Tokenizer ki vocabulary size 30,522 hai aur model ki maximum context size 512 hai. Ek bahut important baat: hamesha wahi tokenizer use karo jiske saath model train hua tha — tokenizer badalna vocabulary ko shuffle karne jaisa hai.

Poora dataset tokenize karna

Poore corpus ko tokenize karne ke liye Dataset ka map() method use hota hai, jo har element par ek processing function lagata hai:

def tokenize(batch):
    return tokenizer(batch["text"], padding=True, truncation=True)
emotions_encoded = emotions.map(tokenize, batched=True, batch_size=None)

padding=True se examples ko batch ke sabse lambe example ke size tak zeros se pad kiya jaata hai, aur truncation=True se examples ko model ki maximum context size tak truncate kiya jaata hai. Padding ke liye [PAD] token hota hai (ID 0), aur khaas tokens me [UNK] (100), [CLS] (101), [SEP] (102) aur [MASK] (103) bhi hain. Padding ke saath tokenizer attention_mask bhi deta hai — isse model ko pata chalta hai ki padded hisse ko ignore karna hai. map() ke baad dataset me input_ids aur attention_mask naam ke naye columns add ho jaate hain.

Yaad rakho: Tokenizer wahi use karo jo model ke saath train hua tha. Subword tokenization rare words ko tod kar aur common words ko poora rakh kar vocabulary ko chhota aur inputs ko manageable rakhta hai — aur attention mask padding ko model se chhupata hai.

02.3Chapter 2 · Text Classification

Trainer API se Fine-Tuning

DistilBERT jaise models masked words predict karne ke liye pretrain hote hain — text classification ke liye unhe thoda modify karna padta hai. Is section me hum pehle model ko feature extractor ki tarah use karenge, phir use end-to-end fine-tune karenge, aur dekhenge ki Trainer API training loop ko kitna aasan bana deti hai.

Architecture: body + classification head

Text tokenize hokar one-hot token encodings banti hain, phir ye token embeddings me badalti hain — lower-dimensional space me rehne wale vectors. Ye embeddings encoder layers se guzarti hain aur har input token ke liye ek hidden state deti hain. Pretraining me har hidden state se masked token predict kiya jaata hai; classification ke liye us language modeling layer ko ek classification layer se replace kar dete hain.

Feature extraction: model ko freeze karo

Feature-based approach me model ke body ke weights ko training ke dauraan freeze kar dete hain aur hidden states ko classifier ke liye features ki tarah use karte hain. Fayda ye hai ki hidden states sirf ek baar precompute karne hote hain, isliye GPU ke bina bhi kaam chal jaata hai. AutoModel.from_pretrained("distilbert-base-uncased") se model load hota hai, aur GPU available ho to model ko .to(device) se GPU par bhej dete hain. Ek string ke last hidden states torch.no_grad() ke andar nikalte hain — isse gradient calculation band ho jaata hai aur memory bachta hai. Output ka shape [batch_size, n_tokens, hidden_dim] hota hai. Classification ke liye aam taur par [CLS] token ka hidden state use hota hai, jo sequence ke start me hota hai. Poore dataset ke hidden states map() se ek baar me nikal kar ek feature matrix banayi jaati hai: train ke liye shape (16000, 768) aur validation ke liye (2000, 768).

Hidden states ko visualize karna

768 dimensions ko dekhna mushkil hai, isliye UMAP algorithm se vectors ko 2D me project kiya jaata hai (pehle MinMaxScaler se [0,1] range me scale karke). Plot me dikhta hai ki negative emotions — sadness, anger, fear — ek hi jagah occupy karte hain, jabki joy aur love unse alag aur ek doosre ke paas hain, aur surprise poori jagah bikhra hua hai.

Simple classifier: logistic regression

Hidden states par Scikit-learn se logistic regression train karte hain — ye tez hai aur GPU nahi chahiye. Validation accuracy 0.633 aati hai. Ye random se thodi behtar lag sakti hai, lekin unbalanced multiclass dataset ke liye ye kaafi behtar hai: ek DummyClassifier jo hamesha sabse frequent class choose karta hai, sirf 0.352 accuracy deta hai. Confusion matrix batati hai ki anger aur fear aksar sadness se confuse hote hain, aur love aur surprise aksar joy se — jo visualization se bhi match karta hai.

Fine-tuning: poora model train karo

Fine-tuning me hidden states ko fixed features ki tarah use nahi karte — poora model classification head ke saath train hota hai, taaki hidden states training ke dauraan task ke liye adapt ho sakein. Iske liye AutoModelForSequenceClassification use hota hai, jisme pretrained model ke upar ek classification head hota hai — bas num_labels=6 batana hota hai. Classification head ke weights randomly initialize hote hain, isliye load karte waqt warning aati hai — ye normal hai.

Metrics aur TrainingArguments

Training ke dauraan metrics monitor karne ke liye ek compute_metrics() function define karte hain jo F1-score aur accuracy compute karti hai. Phir TrainingArguments se hyperparameters set karte hain — output_dir, 2 epochs, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 64, weight decay 0.01, har epoch par evaluation, aur push_to_hub=True taaki model Hub par share ho sake. Hub par login karne ke liye notebook me notebook_login() ya terminal me huggingface-cli login use hota hai. Phir Trainer banakar trainer.train() chalate hain:

trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=training_args,
    compute_metrics=compute_metrics,
    train_dataset=emotions_encoded["train"],
    eval_dataset=emotions_encoded["validation"],
    tokenizer=tokenizer)
trainer.train()

Result shandaar hai: pehle epoch ke baad F1 lagbhag 0.89, doosre ke baad validation accuracy 0.9225 aur F1 0.9226 — feature-based approach se bahut bada improvement. TensorFlow users Keras API se bhi fine-tune kar sakte hain — TFAutoModelForSequenceClassification aur model ki built-in fit() method se.

Yaad rakho: Feature extraction tez aur sasta hai, fine-tuning behtar hai — yahan F1 0.63 accuracy se badh kar 0.92 ho gaya. Trainer API training loop, evaluation aur Hub sharing — teeno ko kuch lines me sambhal leti hai.

def extract_hidden_states(batch):
    # Place model inputs on the GPU
    inputs = {k:v.to(device) for k,v in batch.items() 
              if k in tokenizer.model_input_names}
    # Extract last hidden states
    with torch.no_grad():
        last_hidden_state = model(**inputs).last_hidden_state
    # Return vector for [CLS] token
    return {"hidden_state": last_hidden_state[:,0].cpu().numpy()}

def plot_confusion_matrix(y_preds, y_true, labels):
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_preds, normalize="true")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix=cm, display_labels=labels)
    disp.plot(cmap="Blues", values_format=".2f", ax=ax, colorbar=False)
    plt.title("Normalized confusion matrix")

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score

def compute_metrics(pred):
    labels = pred.label_ids
    preds = pred.predictions.argmax(-1)
    f1 = f1_score(labels, preds, average="weighted")
    acc = accuracy_score(labels, preds)
    return {"accuracy": acc, "f1": f1}

02.4Chapter 2 · Text Classification

Evaluation aur Error Analysis

Model train karna sirf aadha kaam hai — uske baad ye samajhna zaroori hai ki model kahan achha hai, kahan galat hai, aur kyun. Ek achhi accuracy kabhi-kabhi serious flaws ko chhupa sakti hai. Is section me hum evaluation, confusion matrix aur loss-based error analysis dekhenge.

Trainer se predictions lena

trainer.predict() ek PredictionOutput object deta hai jisme predictions, label ids aur metrics hote hain. Validation set par metrics kuch is tarah dikhte hain: test loss lagbhag 0.22, accuracy 0.9225, F1 0.9226. Raw predictions par np.argmax() lagakar predicted labels nikale jaate hain, phir unse confusion matrix plot ki jaati hai. Fine-tuned model ki confusion matrix ideal diagonal ke bahut kareeb hoti hai — love ab bhi aksar joy se confuse hota hai, jo natural lagta hai, aur surprise bhi aksar joy ya fear se confuse hota hai.

Baseline se compare karna

Accuracy ko hamesha ek simple baseline se compare karna chahiye. Yahan majority-class baseline sirf 0.352 deta hai, jabki feature-based logistic regression 0.633 aur fine-tuned model 0.9225 deta hai. Ye comparison batata hai ki improvement asli hai, sirf dataset ki imbalance ka side-effect nahi. Confusion matrix ye bhi batati hai ki kaunsi classes ek doosre se confuse hoti hain — jaise anger aur fear ka sadness se confuse hona, jo UMAP visualization me bhi dikha tha.

Error analysis: loss se sort karo

Ek simple lekin powerful technique hai validation samples ko model loss ke hisaab se sort karna. Forward pass me label dene par loss automatically calculate ho jaata hai. Har sample ka loss nikal kar DataFrame banate hain, phir sabse zyada loss wale examples dekhte hain. Isse do cheezein milti hain:

  • Wrong labels: Labels lagane ki har process me galti ho sakti hai — annotators galti kar sakte hain ya disagree kar sakte hain. Agar labels automatically lagana aasan hota, to model ki zaroorat hi nahi hoti. Is approach se galat labeled examples jaldi mil jaate hain aur unhe correct kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Dataset ki quirks: Real-world datasets hamesha thode messy hote hain. Text me khaas characters ya strings predictions par bada asar daal sakte hain. Model ki sabse kamzor predictions ko dekh kar aise features pehchane ja sakte hain, aur data clean karke ya aise examples add karke model ko zyada robust banaya ja sakta hai.

Sabse zyada loss wale examples kya batate hain

Sabse zyada loss wale examples me kai tweets aise hain jinki class clear hi nahi hai — kuch galat labeled lagte hain, kuch ko ek nayi class ki zaroorat ho sakti hai. Khaas taur par joy class kai baar galat labeled lagti hai. Is jaankari se dataset ko refine kiya ja sakta hai, aur aksar dataset sudharne se utna hi ya usse zyada performance gain milta hai jitna zyada data ya bade model se milta hai.

Sabse kam loss wale examples bhi dekho

Deep learning models prediction tak pahunchne ke liye shortcuts dhoondhne aur exploit karne me bahut achhe hote hain. Isliye sirf galtiyan hi nahi, wo examples bhi dekhne chahiye jin par model sabse confident hai. Yahan model sabse confident sadness class predict karne me tha — lowest-loss examples lagbhag saare sadness ke the. Ye jaanna zaroori hai taaki hum sure rahen ki model text ke kisi galat feature ko exploit to nahi kar raha.

Model ko save aur share karna

Akhir me model ko save aur share karna hota hai. Trainer API se ye aasan hai — trainer.push_to_hub(commit_message="Training completed!") se fine-tuned model Hub par chala jaata hai. Phir use pipeline se seedha use kar sakte ho, bilkul waise hi jaise Chapter 1 me kiya tha:

classifier = pipeline("text-classification", model=model_id)
preds = classifier(custom_tweet, return_all_scores=True)

Ek naye tweet "I saw a movie today and it was really good." par model ne sabse likely class joy batayi, jo reasonable hai. Jab model Hub par push hota hai, to uske liye automatically ek inference endpoint bhi ban jaata hai jise HTTP requests se call kiya ja sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Accuracy ke peeche mat chhupo — confusion matrix dekho, sabse zyada aur sabse kam loss wale examples dekho. Galat labels aur dataset ki quirks aksar model ki galtiyon ki asli wajah hote hain, aur unhe sudharna bade model se zyada fayda de sakta hai.
Full notebook code — 02_classification.ipynb (9 cells)
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/02_classification.ipynb)
from torch.nn.functional import cross_entropy

def forward_pass_with_label(batch):
    # Place all input tensors on the same device as the model
    inputs = {k:v.to(device) for k,v in batch.items() 
              if k in tokenizer.model_input_names}

    with torch.no_grad():
        output = model(**inputs)
        pred_label = torch.argmax(output.logits, axis=-1)
        loss = cross_entropy(output.logits, batch["label"].to(device), 
                             reduction="none")

    # Place outputs on CPU for compatibility with other dataset columns   
    return {"loss": loss.cpu().numpy(), 
            "predicted_label": pred_label.cpu().numpy()}

03Chapter 3 · Transformer Anatomy

Transformer Anatomy — Architecture

Chapter 2 me humne transformer ko fine-tune karna seekha — ab dekhte hain ki ye andar se kaise kaam karta hai. Is chapter me hum PyTorch se Transformer ke main building blocks ko implement karenge, aur samjhenge ki attention, embeddings aur feed-forward layers mil kar kaise kaam karte hain.

Encoder-decoder architecture

Original Transformer encoder-decoder architecture par based hai, jo machine translation jaise tasks ke liye use hoti hai — ek bhasha ke words ki sequence ko doosri bhasha me badalna. Iske do components hain: Encoder, jo input sequence ko tokens ki embedding vectors ki sequence me badalta hai (ise hidden state ya context kehte hain), aur Decoder, jo encoder ke hidden state ka use karke output sequence ko ek-ek token karke generate karta hai.

Architecture ki pehchan

Figure me kuch cheezein turant dikhti hain. Pehle, input text tokenize hokar token embeddings me badalti hai. Kyunki attention mechanism ko tokens ki relative positions ka pata nahi hota, token embeddings ko positional embeddings ke saath combine kiya jaata hai, jo har token ki position ki jaankari deti hain. Doosre, encoder kai encoder layers ka stack hota hai — bilkul waise hi jaise computer vision me convolutional layers stack hote hain — aur decoder ka bhi apna stack hota hai. Teesre, encoder ka output har decoder layer ko milta hai, aur decoder sabse probable agla token predict karta hai. Us output ko wapas decoder me daal kar agla token generate karte hain, jab tak ek khaas end-of-sequence (EOS) token na aa jaye ya maximum length na pahunch jaye. Jaise decoder ne "Die" aur "Zeit" predict kar liye hain, to ab wo in dono aur encoder ke saare outputs ko lekar agla token "fliegt" predict karega.

Teen prakar ke transformer models

Original Transformer sequence-to-sequence tasks ke liye design hua tha, lekin encoder aur decoder blocks ko jald hi standalone models ke roop me adapt kar liya gaya. Aaj saikadon transformer models hain, lekin zyadatar teen types me se ek hain:

  • Encoder-only: Input text ko ek rich numerical representation me badalte hain, jo text classification ya named entity recognition jaise tasks ke liye achha hai. BERT aur uske variants jaise RoBERTa aur DistilBERT is class me aate hain. Kisi token ki representation uske left (pehle) aur right (baad) dono contexts par depend karti hai — ise bidirectional attention kehte hain.
  • Decoder-only: Ek prompt jaise "Thanks for lunch, I had a..." ko aage badha kar agla word predict karte hain. GPT family is class me hai. Yahan token ki representation sirf left context par depend karti hai — ise causal ya autoregressive attention kehte hain.
  • Encoder-decoder: Ek sequence ko doosri sequence me map karte hain — machine translation aur summarization ke liye. Original Transformer ke alawa BART aur T5 is class me aate hain.

Ye distinction thoda blurry bhi hai: GPT jaise decoder-only models ko translation jaise tasks ke liye prime kiya ja sakta hai, aur BERT jaise encoder-only models ko summarization par lagaya ja sakta hai.

Encoder layer ke andar kya hai

Encoder kai encoder layers ka stack hota hai. Har encoder layer ko embeddings ki sequence milti hai aur wo unhe do sublayers se guzarta hai: ek multi-head self-attention layer, aur ek fully connected feed-forward layer jo har input embedding par apply hota hai. Har layer ki output embeddings ka size input ke barabar hota hai, aur encoder stack ka main kaam input embeddings ko "update" karna hai taaki unme sequence ki contextual jaankari aa jaye. Jaise "apple" word "keynote" ya "phone" ke paas ho to wo zyada "company-like" aur kam "fruit-like" ho jaata hai. Dono sublayers me skip connections aur layer normalization bhi use hote hain, jo deep networks ko effectively train karne ke standard tricks hain.

Yaad rakho: Encoder samajhta hai, decoder generate karta hai, aur dono mil kar translate karte hain. Har transformer model in teen families me se ek hai — encoder-only, decoder-only, ya encoder-decoder.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Transformer Anatomy
← Previous02.4 · Evaluation aur Error Analysis→ Next03.1 · Attention Mechanism — Self-Attention
03.1Chapter 3 · Transformer Anatomy

Attention Mechanism — Self-Attention

Self-attention Transformer ka sabse important building block hai. Iska idea simple hai: har token ke liye ek fixed embedding use karne ke bajaye, poori sequence ka use karke har embedding ka ek weighted average banao — taaki har token ki representation me uska context aa jaye.

Contextualized embeddings

Self-attention me weights ek hi set ke saare hidden states ke liye compute hote hain. Mathematically, har nayi embedding saare token embeddings ka weighted average hoti hai, aur weights ka sum 1 hota hai. Example se samjho: "flies" dekh kar aapko annoying insects yaad aa sakte hain, lekin "time flies like an arrow" me context se pata chalta hai ki "flies" ek verb hai. "Time" aur "arrow" ko zyada weight de kar "flies" ki aisi representation banayi ja sakti hai jo context ko capture kare. Aisi embeddings ko contextualized embeddings kehte hain.

Scaled dot-product attention: chaar steps

Self-attention implement karne ka sabse common tareeka scaled dot-product attention hai, jiske chaar steps hain:

  1. Project karo: Har token embedding ko teen vectors me project karo — query, key aur value.
  2. Attention scores: Query aur key vectors ke beech similarity nikalo. Scaled dot-product attention me similarity function dot product hota hai, jo matrix multiplication se efficiently compute hota hai. Similar query aur key ka dot product bada hota hai. n input tokens ke liye n x n matrix of attention scores banti hai.
  3. Attention weights: Dot products bahut bade numbers de sakte hain, jo training ko unstable kar dete hain. Isliye scores ko pehle ek scaling factor se multiply karke unki variance normalize ki jaati hai, phir softmax lagakar ensure kiya jaata hai ki har column ka sum 1 ho. Result n x n matrix me saare attention weights hote hain.
  4. Embeddings update karo: Attention weights ko value vectors se multiply karke har token ki updated representation milti hai.

Poora process sirf do matrix multiplications aur ek softmax hai:

def scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value):
    dim_k = query.size(-1)
    scores = torch.bmm(query, key.transpose(1, 2)) / sqrt(dim_k)
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return torch.bmm(weights, value)

Query, key, value ko ek analogy se samjho

Query, key aur value ke naam information retrieval systems se aaye hain, lekin ek simple analogy se samajh aata hai: maan lo aap supermarket me dinner ke ingredients khareed rahe ho. Aapki recipe ke har ingredient ko ek query samjho. Shelves par labels (keys) dekh kar aap check karte ho ki kaunsa label aapke ingredient se match karta hai (similarity function). Match mile to aap item (value) utha lete ho. Self-attention iska ek "smooth" version hai: har label ingredient se utna match karta hai jitna key query se match karta hai.

Multi-head attention

Practice me self-attention layer har embedding par teen independent linear transformations lagata hai, jo query, key aur value vectors banate hain — har projection ke apne learnable parameters hote hain, jisse layer sequence ke alag-alag semantic aspects par focus kar sakti hai. Isse aage, multiple sets of linear projections use hote hain — har set ek attention head hota hai. Ek head ka softmax aam taur par similarity ke ek hi aspect par focus karta hai; kai heads se model ek saath kai aspects par focus kar sakta hai. Jaise ek head subject-verb interaction par focus kare, doosra paas wale adjectives par. Ye relations data se seekhe jaate hain, hum handcraft nahi karte. BERT me 12 attention heads hain, isliye har head ki dimension 768 / 12 = 64 hoti hai.

Visualization se kya dikhta hai

Attention weights ko visualize karne se pata chalta hai ki model kya seekh raha hai. Do sentences — "time flies like an arrow" aur "fruit flies like a banana" — par "flies" word ke liye pehle sentence me "arrow" important hota hai aur doosre me "fruit" aur "banana". In weights ki wajah se model "flies" ko verb ya noun ke roop me context ke hisaab se alag kar pata hai.

Yaad rakho: Self-attention har token ko poori sequence ka weighted average bana kar context deta hai. Query poochta hai, key match karta hai, value deta hai — aur multiple heads alag-alag tarah ke relationships ek saath seekhte hain.

def scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value):

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class AttentionHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, head_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.q = nn.Linear(embed_dim, head_dim)
        self.k = nn.Linear(embed_dim, head_dim)
        self.v = nn.Linear(embed_dim, head_dim)

    def forward(self, hidden_state):
        attn_outputs = scaled_dot_product_attention(
            self.q(hidden_state), self.k(hidden_state), self.v(hidden_state))
        return attn_outputs
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        embed_dim = config.hidden_size
        num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
        head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList(
            [AttentionHead(embed_dim, head_dim) for _ in range(num_heads)]
        )
        self.output_linear = nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, hidden_state):
        x = torch.cat([h(hidden_state) for h in self.heads], dim=-1)
        x = self.output_linear(x)
        return x

03.2Chapter 3 · Transformer Anatomy

Encoder, Decoder aur Encoder-Decoder

Encoder aur decoder dono Transformer ke building blocks hain, lekin unke kaam alag hain. Encoder input ko samajhta hai, decoder output ko generate karta hai, aur in dono ko jodne ke liye ek khaas attention layer hoti hai. Is section me hum teeno ko implement karne ke nazariye se dekhenge.

Encoder layer ko jodna

Encoder layer me do main sublayers hote hain — multi-head self-attention aur position-wise feed-forward — aur dono ke saath skip connections aur layer normalization use hote hain. Layer normalization ko rakhne ke do tareeke hain — post-norm (original paper wala, skip connections ke beech me, jisme learning rate warm-up chahiye hota hai) aur pre-norm (skip connections ke andar, zyada stable, aaj sabse common). Kitab me pre-norm use kiya gaya hai:

class TransformerEncoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer_norm_1 = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
        self.layer_norm_2 = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
        self.attention = MultiHeadAttention(config)
        self.feed_forward = FeedForward(config)
    def forward(self, x):
        hidden_state = self.layer_norm_1(x)
        x = x + self.attention(hidden_state)
        x = x + self.feed_forward(self.layer_norm_2(x))
        return x

Classification head lagana

Transformer models aam taur par ek task-independent body aur ek task-specific head me bante hote hain. Ab tak humne body banayi hai; text classifier banane ke liye us par ek classification head lagana hota hai. Hamare paas har token ka hidden state hai, lekin sirf ek prediction karni hai. Traditional tareeka hai pehle token ([CLS]) ka hidden state lena aur us par dropout aur ek linear layer lagana:

class TransformerForSequenceClassification(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = TransformerEncoder(config)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.num_labels)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.encoder(x)[:, 0, :]
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

3 classes ke liye output ka shape [1, 3] hota hai — har class ka unnormalized logit.

Decoder: encoder se kya alag hai

Decoder me encoder se ek main farq hai: isme do attention sublayers hote hain. Pehli hai masked multi-head self-attention layer — ye ensure karti hai ki har timestep par generate kiye gaye tokens sirf pehle wale outputs aur current token par based hon. Iske bina decoder training ke dauraan target translations ko copy karke cheat kar sakta tha; masking se task trivial nahi rehta. Doosri hai encoder-decoder attention layer — ye encoder stack ke output key aur value vectors par multi-head attention karti hai, jisme decoder ki intermediate representations queries ka kaam karti hain. Is tarah ye layer do alag sequences — jaise do alag bhashaon — ke tokens ke beech sambandh seekhti hai. Decoder ko har block me encoder ke keys aur values tak access milta hai.

Masking kaise kaam karti hai

Masked self-attention ka trick ek mask matrix hai jisme lower diagonal par ones aur upar zeros hote hain — torch.tril() se banayi jaati hai. Phir masked_fill() se saare zeros ko negative infinity se replace kar dete hain. Softmax lene par in weights ka value zero ho jaata hai, kyunki e ki power negative infinity zero hoti hai. Scaled dot-product attention me ye ek chhota sa badlav hai:

def scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value, mask=None):
    dim_k = query.size(-1)
    scores = torch.bmm(query, key.transpose(1, 2)) / sqrt(dim_k)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float("-inf"))
    weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return weights.bmm(value)

Encoder-decoder attention ko ek analogy se samjho

Maan lo aap (decoder) class me exam de rahe ho, aur aapko pehle wale words ke basis par agla word predict karna hai — bahut mushkil kaam. Aapke bagal wale (encoder) ke paas poora text hai, lekin wo ek foreign exchange student hai aur text uski mother tongue me hai. Aap ek chhota cartoon bana kar (query) use dete ho, wo samajhta hai ki kaunsa passage is description se match karta hai (key), phir us passage ke baad wale word ka cartoon (value) bana kar wapas deta hai. Is system se aap exam me pass ho jaate ho.

Yaad rakho: Encoder = samajhna, decoder = generate karna, aur masked attention decoder ko future dekhne se rokta hai. Body task-independent hoti hai, head task-specific — head badal kar ek hi body se classification, NER ya question answering kiya ja sakta hai.

03.3Chapter 3 · Transformer Anatomy

Positional Embeddings aur Feed-Forward

Self-attention aur feed-forward layers me ek badi kami hai: ye tokens ki position se bilkul invariant hote hain. Attention effectively ek fancy weighted sum hai, isliye token position ki jaankari kho jaati hai. Is section me hum dekhenge ki positional embeddings ye jaankari wapas kaise laate hain, aur feed-forward layer kya karta hai.

Problem: position ki jaankari kho jaati hai

Technical bhasha me, self-attention aur feed-forward layers permutation equivariant hote hain — agar input ko permute kar do, to output bhi bilkul waise hi permute ho jaata hai. Matlab model ko ye pata hi nahi chalta ki kaunsa token pehle aaya aur kaunsa baad me. Text ki sequential nature ko model karne ke liye position ki jaankari inject karni hi padti hai.

Positional embeddings: idea

Positional embeddings ka idea simple lekin bahut effective hai: token embeddings me ek position-dependent pattern of values jod do. Agar har position ka pattern characteristic ho, to attention heads aur feed-forward layers apne transformations me positional jaankari ko incorporate karna seekh sakte hain.

Learnable positional embeddings

Sabse popular approaches me se ek hai learnable pattern use karna, khaas taur par jab pretraining dataset kaafi bada ho. Ye bilkul token embeddings jaisa kaam karta hai, lekin token ID ke bajaye position index ko input le kar. Pretraining ke dauraan positions ko encode karne ka ek efficient tareeka seekh liya jaata hai. Ek custom Embeddings module token embedding layer aur positional embedding layer ko combine karta hai — result sirf dono embeddings ka sum hota hai, uske baad layer normalization aur dropout:

class Embeddings(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_embeddings = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size,
            config.hidden_size)
        self.position_embeddings = nn.Embedding(
            config.max_position_embeddings, config.hidden_size)
        self.layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=1e-12)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout()
    def forward(self, input_ids):
        seq_length = input_ids.size(1)
        position_ids = torch.arange(seq_length).unsqueeze(0)
        embeddings = self.token_embeddings(input_ids)
        embeddings += self.position_embeddings(position_ids)
        return self.dropout(self.layer_norm(embeddings))

Doosre tareeke: absolute aur relative

Learnable embeddings ke alawa do aur approaches hain. Absolute positional representations me modulated sine aur cosine signals ke static patterns se token positions encode kiye jaate hain — ye khaas taur par achha kaam karta hai jab zyada data available na ho. Relative positional representations is intuition par based hain ki embedding compute karte waqt aas-paas ke tokens sabse important hote hain — ye tokens ke beech ki relative positions ko encode karte hain. Ye sirf shuruaat me ek embedding layer add karke set nahi kiya ja sakta, kyunki relative embedding har token ke liye badalti hai; iske liye attention mechanism ko hi modify karna padta hai, extra terms ke saath. Kuch models relative representations use karte hain. Absolute aur relative dono ko combine karke rotary position embeddings banaye jaate hain, jo kai tasks par excellent results dete hain.

Feed-forward layer

Encoder aur decoder me feed-forward sublayer ek simple two-layer fully connected neural network hai, lekin ek twist ke saath: poori sequence ko ek single vector ki tarah process karne ke bajaye, ye har embedding ko independently process karta hai — isliye ise position-wise feed-forward layer kehte hain. Computer vision background wale log ise kernel size one wala one-dimensional convolution bhi kehte hain. Literature se rule of thumb hai ki pehle layer ki hidden size embeddings ki size se chaar guna ho, aur GELU activation function sabse commonly use hota hai. Yahi wo jagah hai jahan model ki zyada capacity aur memorization hoti hai, aur models ko scale up karte waqt isi hisse ko sabse zyada scale kiya jaata hai:

class FeedForward(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size,
            config.intermediate_size)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(config.intermediate_size,
            config.hidden_size)
        self.gelu = nn.GELU()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)

Ek nn.Linear layer aam taur par (batch_size, input_dim) shape ke tensor par kaam karti hai, lekin asal me ye last dimension ke alawa har dimension par independently kaam karti hai — isliye (batch_size, seq_len, hidden_dim) shape ke tensor par ye har token embedding par alag se apply hoti hai, jo bilkul wahi hai jo hum chahte hain. Output ka shape input ke barabar rehta hai: [1, 5, 768].

Yaad rakho: Attention ko order ka pata nahi hota — positional embeddings use ye batate hain. Feed-forward layer har token par alag se kaam karta hai aur model ki capacity ka zyada hissa yahin hota hai. Token + position embeddings ka sum hi encoder ka input hota hai.
Full notebook code — 03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb (10 cells)
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class FeedForward(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.intermediate_size)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(config.intermediate_size, config.hidden_size)
        self.gelu = nn.GELU()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)
        
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.linear_1(x)
        x = self.gelu(x)
        x = self.linear_2(x)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        return x
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)

ff_outputs = feed_forward(attn_outputs)

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class TransformerEncoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer_norm_1 = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
        self.layer_norm_2 = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size)
        self.attention = MultiHeadAttention(config)
        self.feed_forward = FeedForward(config)

    def forward(self, x):
        # Apply layer normalization and then copy input into query, key, value
        hidden_state = self.layer_norm_1(x)
        # Apply attention with a skip connection
        x = x + self.attention(hidden_state)
        # Apply feed-forward layer with a skip connection
        x = x + self.feed_forward(self.layer_norm_2(x))
        return x
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)

inputs_embeds.shape, encoder_layer(inputs_embeds).size()
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class Embeddings(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_embeddings = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, 
                                             config.hidden_size)
        self.position_embeddings = nn.Embedding(config.max_position_embeddings,
                                                config.hidden_size)
        self.layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=1e-12)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout()

    def forward(self, input_ids):
        # Create position IDs for input sequence
        seq_length = input_ids.size(1)
        position_ids = torch.arange(seq_length, dtype=torch.long).unsqueeze(0)
        # Create token and position embeddings
        token_embeddings = self.token_embeddings(input_ids)
        position_embeddings = self.position_embeddings(position_ids)
        # Combine token and position embeddings
        embeddings = token_embeddings + position_embeddings
        embeddings = self.layer_norm(embeddings)
        embeddings = self.dropout(embeddings)
        return embeddings
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)

embedding_layer(inputs.input_ids).size()
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/03_transformer-anatomy.ipynb)
class TransformerEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.embeddings = Embeddings(config)
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([TransformerEncoderLayer(config) 
                                     for _ in range(config.num_hidden_layers)])

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.embeddings(x)
        for layer in self.layers:
            x = layer(x)
        return x

class TransformerForSequenceClassification(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = TransformerEncoder(config)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.num_labels)
        
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.encoder(x)[:, 0, :] # select hidden state of [CLS] token
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

03.4Chapter 3 · Transformer Anatomy

Model Families — BERT, GPT, T5

Teen main architectures ke aas-paas models ka ek poora zoo ban gaya hai — alag datasets, alag sizes, naye pretraining objectives aur architecture me tweaks. Is section me hum transformer family tree ki main branches aur unke important models ko dekhenge.

Encoder branch: BERT aur uske variants

Pehla encoder-only model BERT tha. Ye masked language modeling (MLM) — masked tokens ko predict karna — aur next sentence prediction (NSP) — kya ek text passage doosre ke baad aane ki sambhavna hai — in do objectives se pretrain hua tha. Us waqt isne GLUE benchmark (natural language understanding ko kai tasks par measure karne wala) par saare state-of-the-art models ko peeche chhod diya tha. Uske baad BERT ko aur behtar banaya gaya:

  • DistilBERT: Knowledge distillation se BERT ki 97% performance deta hai, lekin 40% kam memory use karta hai aur 60% tez hai — low latency wale deployments ke liye perfect.
  • RoBERTa: BERT ko lamba train karke, bade batches aur zyada data ke saath, aur NSP task ko hata kar, performance ko significantly behtar banaya gaya.
  • XLM: Multilingual models ke liye kai pretraining objectives explore kiye, jinme translation language modeling (TLM) bhi tha.
  • XLM-RoBERTa (XLM-R): Common Crawl corpus se 2.5 terabytes text ka dataset bana kar MLM se train kiya gaya — bina parallel texts ke. Ye XLM aur multilingual BERT variants ko bade margin se harata hai, khaas taur par low-resource languages par.
  • ALBERT: Embedding aur hidden dimensions ko alag karke aur saari layers me parameters share karke kam parameters me bade models train karta hai; NSP ki jagah sentence-ordering prediction use karta hai.
  • ELECTRA: Do models use karta hai — ek chhota model masked tokens predict karta hai, aur discriminator predict karta hai ki kaunse tokens originally masked the — isse training 30 guna zyada efficient ho jaati hai.
  • DeBERTa: Har token ko content aur relative position ke liye do vectors se represent karta hai; ye SuperGLUE par human baseline ko beat karne wala pehla model tha.

Decoder branch: GPT family

Decoder models ki progress me bade datasets aur bade language models ka bada haath hai. Ye models agla word predict karne me exceptionally achhe hain aur zyadatar text generation ke liye use hote hain:

  • GPT: Transformer decoder architecture aur transfer learning ko combine kiya — BookCorpus par next-word prediction se pretrain hua.
  • GPT-2: Model aur training set ko upscale kiya — ye lambi coherent text generate kar sakta tha, aur misuse ki concerns ki wajah se staged fashion me release hua.
  • CTRL: Sequence ke shuruaat me "control tokens" add karke generated text ki style ko control karne ki suvidha di.
  • GPT-3: GPT-2 ko 100 guna upscale karke banaya gaya — 175 billion parameters. Ye realistic text generate karta hai aur few-shot learning dikhata hai.
  • GPT-Neo / GPT-J-6B: GPT-3 scale ke models ko recreate aur release karne ke liye ek researchers ke collective ne banaye — 1.3, 2.7 aur 6 billion parameters wale variants.

Encoder-decoder branch

  • T5: Saare NLU aur NLG tasks ko text-to-text tasks me convert kar deta hai — text classification me bhi decoder ko label ko normal text ki tarah generate karna hota hai. Sabse bada 11 billion parameters wala model kai benchmarks par state-of-the-art raha.
  • BART: BERT aur GPT ke pretraining procedures ko combine karta hai — input ko corrupt karke (mask, permute, delete) decoder se original text reconstruct karwata hai; NLU aur NLG dono me state-of-the-art.
  • M2M-100: Pehla translation model jo kisi bhi 100 languages ke beech translate kar sakta hai — rare aur underrepresented languages ke beech bhi high-quality translations. Source aur target language batane ke liye prefix tokens use karta hai.
  • BigBird: Attention ki quadratic memory requirement ki wajah se context size limited hoti hai. BigBird sparse attention use karta hai jo linearly scale hoti hai — context 512 tokens se badh kar 4,096 ho jaata hai, jo text summarization jaise tasks me bahut kaam aata hai.
Yaad rakho: Encoder = samajhna (BERT family), decoder = generate karna (GPT family), encoder-decoder = ek sequence ko doosri me badalna (T5, BART). Saare models ke pretrained checkpoints Hub par milte hain aur Chapter 2 wale tareeke se fine-tune kiye ja sakte hain.
SOURCESource: Natural Language Processing with Transformers, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Transformer Anatomy

04Chapter 4 · Multilingual Named Entity Recognition

Multilingual Named Entity Recognition

Ab tak humne transformers ko English corpora par lagaya — lekin jab documents Greek, Swahili ya kisi aur bhasha me hon to kya karoge? Pretrained models zyadatar high-resource languages jaise German, Russian ya Mandarin ke liye hi milte hain. Aur agar corpus multilingual ho, to har bhasha ke liye alag model maintain karna production me kisi ke liye mazedaar nahi hoga. Iska hal hai multilingual transformers.

Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer kya hai

Multilingual transformers masked language modeling se pretrain hote hain, lekin 100 se zyada bhashaon ke texts par jointly train hote hain. Bade corpora par kai bhashaon me pretrain karne se in models me zero-shot cross-lingual transfer ki ability aa jaati hai — matlab ek bhasha par fine-tune kiya gaya model bina kisi aur training ke doosri bhashaon par bhi apply ho sakta hai. Ye models code-switching ke liye bhi achhe hain, jahan ek speaker ek hi conversation me do ya zyada bhashaon ke beech switch karta hai. Is chapter me hum XLM-RoBERTa (XLM-R) naam ke ek model ko fine-tune karenge, jo kai bhashaon me named entity recognition (NER) kar sakta hai.

Task: Swiss customer ke liye NER

Maan lo hum Switzerland ke ek customer ke liye NER karna chahte hain, jahan chaar national languages hain (aur English aksar unke beech bridge ka kaam karta hai). NER wo task hai jo text me people, organizations ya locations jaise entities ko pehchanta hai. Ye entities company documents se insights nikalne, search engines ki quality badhane, ya corpus se ek structured database banane ke liye use ho sakti hain.

Dataset: PAN-X (WikiANN)

Hum XTREME benchmark ke ek subset ka use karenge jise WikiANN ya PAN-X kehte hain. Ye dataset kai bhashaon ke Wikipedia articles se bana hai, jinme Switzerland ki chaar sabse common bhashaen hain: German (62.9%), French (22.9%), Italian (8.4%) aur English (5.9%). Har article me LOC (location), PER (person) aur ORG (organization) tags "inside-outside-beginning" (IOB2) format me annotated hain. IOB2 me B- prefix entity ki shuruaat batata hai, usi entity ke aage wale tokens ko I- prefix milta hai, aur O tag ka matlab hai ki token kisi entity ka hissa nahi hai. Jaise "[Name] ek computer scientist hai [Company] me [Place] me" wale sentence me pehle do tokens ko B-PER aur I-PER, company ko B-ORG aur jagah ko B-LOC milega.

Swiss corpus banana

XTREME ke 183 configurations hain; PAN-X subsets ko get_dataset_config_names("xtreme") se dhoondha ja sakta hai — har subset ka naam PAN-X.de jaise format me hota hai, jahan suffix ISO 639-1 language code hai. Hum chaaron bhashaon ke corpora ko unke spoken proportions ke hisaab se sample karenge — ye jaan-boojh kar ek language imbalance banata hai, jo real-world datasets me bahut common hai, kyunki minority language me labeled examples jama karna mehenga hota hai (fluent domain experts ki kami ki wajah se). Training examples ki sankhya: German 12,580, French 4,580, Italian 1,680 aur English 1,180. Design se German ke examples baaki sab bhashaon ke combined se zyada hain, isliye hum ise zero-shot transfer ka starting point banayenge.

Tags ko readable banana

Har example me tokens, ner_tags aur langs columns hote hain. ner_tags ek ClassLabel hai jisme 7 classes hain: O, B-PER, I-PER, B-ORG, I-ORG, B-LOC, I-LOC. map() aur int2str() se ek naya column ner_tags_str banaya jaata hai jisme tags readable format me hon. Tags ki frequencies check karne par pata chalta hai ki PER, LOC aur ORG ka distribution har split me lagbhag ek jaisa hai — isliye validation aur test sets model ki generalize karne ki ability ka achha measure denge.

Yaad rakho: Multilingual transformers 100+ bhashaon par jointly pretrain hote hain, isliye ek bhasha par fine-tune karke doosri par use kiya ja sakta hai. IOB2 format me B- shuruaat, I- continuation aur O non-entity batata hai.

import numpy as np

def align_predictions(predictions, label_ids):
    preds = np.argmax(predictions, axis=2)
    batch_size, seq_len = preds.shape
    labels_list, preds_list = [], []

    for batch_idx in range(batch_size):
        example_labels, example_preds = [], []
        for seq_idx in range(seq_len):
            # Ignore label IDs = -100
            if label_ids[batch_idx, seq_idx] != -100:
                example_labels.append(index2tag[label_ids[batch_idx][seq_idx]])
                example_preds.append(index2tag[preds[batch_idx][seq_idx]])

        labels_list.append(example_labels)
        preds_list.append(example_preds)

    return preds_list, labels_list

from torch.nn.functional import cross_entropy

def forward_pass_with_label(batch):
    # Convert dict of lists to list of dicts suitable for data collator
    features = [dict(zip(batch, t)) for t in zip(*batch.values())]
    # Pad inputs and labels and put all tensors on device
    batch = data_collator(features)
    input_ids = batch["input_ids"].to(device)
    attention_mask = batch["attention_mask"].to(device)
    labels = batch["labels"].to(device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        # Pass data through model  
        output = trainer.model(input_ids, attention_mask)
        # Logit.size: [batch_size, sequence_length, classes]
        # Predict class with largest logit value on classes axis
        predicted_label = torch.argmax(output.logits, axis=-1).cpu().numpy()
    # Calculate loss per token after flattening batch dimension with view
    loss = cross_entropy(output.logits.view(-1, 7), 
                         labels.view(-1), reduction="none")
    # Unflatten batch dimension and convert to numpy array
    loss = loss.view(len(input_ids), -1).cpu().numpy()

    return {"loss":loss, "predicted_label": predicted_label}

from sklearn.metrics import ConfusionMatrixDisplay, confusion_matrix

def plot_confusion_matrix(y_preds, y_true, labels):
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_preds, normalize="true")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix=cm, display_labels=labels)

def get_samples(df):
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        labels, preds, tokens, losses = [], [], [], []
        for i, mask in enumerate(row["attention_mask"]):

04.1Chapter 4 · Multilingual Named Entity Recognition

Token Classification kya hai?

Chapter 2 me text classification ke liye poori sequence ki ek hi representation ([CLS] token) ko ek dense layer se guzara gaya tha. NER me approach similar hai, lekin ek farq ke saath: har individual input token ki representation ko ek hi fully connected layer se guzara jaata hai, taaki har token ki entity predict ho sake. Isliye NER ko aksar token classification task ke roop me frame kiya jaata hai.

Subwords ko label kaise dein?

Yahan ek mushkil sawaal aata hai: subwords ko kaise handle karein? Jaise ek naam do subwords me toot jaaye — pehla hissa aur doosra hissa — to B-PER label kis ko mile? Original BERT paper me pehle subword ko label diya gaya aur baad wale subword ko ignore kiya gaya. Yahi convention hum bhi adopt karenge, aur ignored subwords ko IGN se mark karenge. Baad wale subword ko B-LOC jaisa label ki copy dena IOB2 format ko violate karta.

Body aur head: Transformers ka design pattern

Transformers ki versatility ka main concept architecture ko body aur head me baantna hai. Body token embeddings aur transformer layers hoti hai — ye task-agnostic hoti hai. Head task-specific last layer hoti hai. Code me body BertModel ya GPT2Model jaise classes me implement hoti hai jo last layer ke hidden states deti hain, aur task-specific models jaise BertForMaskedLM ya BertForSequenceClassification base model par zaroori head add karte hain.

Apna custom token classification model banana

Agar aapke task ke liye koi ForTask class na ho, to ghabrana nahi — Transformers ko is tarah design kiya gaya hai ki aap existing models ko aasani se extend kar sakte ho. Hum XLM-R ke liye ek custom token classification head banayenge. XLM-R ka architecture RoBERTa jaisa hai, isliye base model ke taur par RobertaModel use hota hai:

class XLMRobertaForTokenClassification(RobertaPreTrainedModel):
    config_class = XLMRobertaConfig
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__(config)
        self.num_labels = config.num_labels
        self.roberta = RobertaModel(config, add_pooling_layer=False)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size,
            config.num_labels)
        self.init_weights()

add_pooling_layer=False ensure karta hai ki sirf [CLS] token ka hidden state nahi, saare hidden states return hon. forward() method me data pehle body se guzarta hai, phir hidden state dropout aur classification layers se, aur agar labels diye gaye hon to loss bhi calculate hota hai — nn.CrossEntropyLoss() se. Output ko TokenClassifierOutput object me wrap kiya jaata hai. RobertaPreTrainedModel se inherit karne ki wajah se hume from_pretrained() jaisi utilities muft me mil jaati hain.

Custom model load karna

Model load karne ke liye tags ki mapping chahiye hoti hai — index2tag aur tag2index — aur classes ki sankhya. Ye sab AutoConfig object me store hota hai, aur from_pretrained() ko keyword arguments de kar default values override ki ja sakti hain:

xlmr_config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(xlmr_model_name,
    num_labels=tags.num_classes,
    id2label=index2tag, label2id=tag2index)
xlmr_model = XLMRobertaForTokenClassification.from_pretrained(
    xlmr_model_name, config=xlmr_config).to(device)

Pehle test me model ke logits ka shape [batch_size, num_tokens, num_tags] hota hai — har token ko 7 possible NER tags me se ek logit milta hai. Random weights wali classification layer ke predictions naturally bekar hote hain; fine-tuning se ye behtar honge.

NER ke liye tokenize karna: labels ko align karna

Training se pehle inputs ko tokenize karna aur labels ko prepare karna hota hai. Tokenizer ko is_split_into_words=True batate hain ki input pehle se words me split hai. Phir word_ids() function har subword ko words sequence ke corresponding index se map karti hai — special tokens jaise <s> aur </s> ko None milta hai. Label IDs banane ka rule simple hai: agar word index None hai ya pehle wale word ke barabar hai, to label -100 do; warna us word ka asli label do. -100 isliye chuna gaya kyunki PyTorch ki CrossEntropyLoss me ignore_index ka value -100 hota hai — ye index training ke dauraan ignore ho jaata hai, isliye consecutive subwords ko loss se bahar rakha ja sakta hai. Ye logic tokenize_and_align_labels() function me wrap karke poore dataset par map() se apply kiya jaata hai.

Yaad rakho: NER = token classification: har token ko ek label. Sirf pehle subword ko label do, baaki ko -100 se ignore karo. Body aur head ka separation hi aapko kisi bhi task ke liye custom model banane deta hai.

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/04_multilingual-ner.ipynb)
import torch.nn as nn
from transformers import XLMRobertaConfig
from transformers.modeling_outputs import TokenClassifierOutput
from transformers.models.roberta.modeling_roberta import RobertaModel
from transformers.models.roberta.modeling_roberta import RobertaPreTrainedModel

class XLMRobertaForTokenClassification(RobertaPreTrainedModel):
    config_class = XLMRobertaConfig

    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__(config)
        self.num_labels = config.num_labels
        # Load model body
        self.roberta = RobertaModel(config, add_pooling_layer=False)
        # Set up token classification head
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.hidden_dropout_prob)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.num_labels)
        # Load and initialize weights
        self.init_weights()

    def forward(self, input_ids=None, attention_mask=None, token_type_ids=None, 
                labels=None, **kwargs):
        # Use model body to get encoder representations
        outputs = self.roberta(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask,
                               token_type_ids=token_type_ids, **kwargs)
        # Apply classifier to encoder representation
        sequence_output = self.dropout(outputs[0])
        logits = self.classifier(sequence_output)
        # Calculate losses
        loss = None
        if labels is not None:
            loss_fct = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
            loss = loss_fct(logits.view(-1, self.num_labels), labels.view(-1))
        # Return model output object
        return TokenClassifierOutput(loss=loss, logits=logits, 
                                     hidden_states=outputs.hidden_states, 
                                     attentions=outputs.attentions)

def tag_text(text, tags, model, tokenizer):
    # Get tokens with special characters
    tokens = tokenizer(text).tokens()
    # Encode the sequence into IDs
    input_ids = xlmr_tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to(device)
    # Get predictions as distribution over 7 possible classes
    outputs = model(input_ids)[0]
    # Take argmax to get most likely class per token
    predictions = torch.argmax(outputs, dim=2)
    # Convert to DataFrame
    preds = [tags.names[p] for p in predictions[0].cpu().numpy()]
    return pd.DataFrame([tokens, preds], index=["Tokens", "Tags"])
