Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/04_multilingual-ner.ipynb)
def tokenize_and_align_labels(examples):
    tokenized_inputs = xlmr_tokenizer(examples["tokens"], truncation=True, 
                                      is_split_into_words=True)
    labels = []
    for idx, label in enumerate(examples["ner_tags"]):
        word_ids = tokenized_inputs.word_ids(batch_index=idx)
        previous_word_idx = None
        label_ids = []
        for word_idx in word_ids:
            if word_idx is None or word_idx == previous_word_idx:
                label_ids.append(-100)
            else:
                label_ids.append(label[word_idx])
            previous_word_idx = word_idx
        labels.append(label_ids)
    tokenized_inputs["labels"] = labels
    return tokenized_inputs
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/04_multilingual-ner.ipynb)
def encode_panx_dataset(corpus):
    return corpus.map(tokenize_and_align_labels, batched=True, 
                      remove_columns=['langs', 'ner_tags', 'tokens'])

04.2Chapter 4 · Multilingual Named Entity Recognition

XLM-R aur Multilingual Models

Multilingual transformers apne monolingual counterparts jaisi hi architecture aur training procedure use karte hain — farq sirf itna hai ki pretraining corpus kai bhashaon ke documents se bana hota hai.

mBERT se XLM-R tak

Pehle multilingual transformers me se ek mBERT tha, jo BERT jaisi hi architecture aur pretraining objective use karta tha, lekin pretraining corpus me kai bhashaon ke Wikipedia articles add kar diye gaye the. Uske baad se mBERT ko XLM-RoBERTa (XLM-R) ne peeche chhod diya hai. XLM-R sirf MLM ko pretraining objective ke taur par use karta hai, 100 bhashaon ke liye, lekin iski khaasiyat iske pretraining corpus ka huge size hai: har bhasha ke Wikipedia dumps aur web se 2.5 terabytes Common Crawl data. Ye corpus pehle wale models se kai orders of magnitude bada hai, aur low-resource languages jaise Burmese aur Swahili ke liye signal me bada boost deta hai, jahan Wikipedia articles bahut kam hain. Naam ka RoBERTa hissa isliye hai kyunki pretraining approach monolingual RoBERTa jaisi hai (next sentence prediction task hata kar). XLM-R language embeddings drop karta hai aur SentencePiece use karta hai. Ek notable farq vocabulary ka size hai: XLM-R ki 250,000 tokens, jabki RoBERTa ki sirf 55,000.

Evaluation ke teen tareeke

Cross-lingual transfer ki progress measure karne ke liye CoNLL-2002 aur CoNLL-2003 datasets aksar benchmark ke taur par use hote hain — ye English, Dutch, Spanish aur German ke news articles hain, jinme PAN-X wale LOC, PER aur ORG categories ke alawa ek MISC label bhi hai. Models ko aam taur par teen tareekon se evaluate kiya jaata hai: English par fine-tune karke har bhasha par test karna, har bhasha par alag se, ya saare data par ek saath. Hum isi strategy ko adopt karenge.

SentencePiece tokenizer: WordPiece se kya alag hai

BERT WordPiece use karta hai, XLM-R SentencePiece use karta hai — jo saare 100 bhashaon ke raw text par train hota hai. Ek hi sentence "The sparrow loves New York!" ko dono tokenizers se encode karne par farq saaf dikhta hai. BERT tokens hote hain: [CLS] The spa ##rrow loves New York ! [SEP]. XLM-R tokens hote hain: <s> _The _Spar row _love s _New _York ! </s>. XLM-R [CLS] aur [SEP] ke bajaye <s> aur </s> use karta hai sequence ki shuruaat aur end ke liye. SentencePiece Unigram subword segmentation par based hai aur har input text ko Unicode characters ki sequence ke taur par encode karta hai — isliye ye accents aur punctuation se agnostic hai, aur Japanese jaise bhashaon me bhi kaam karta hai jahan whitespace nahi hota. Whitespace ko Unicode symbol U+2581 (_) se represent kiya jaata hai, isliye detokenize bina ambiguity ke ho jaata hai — WordPiece "York" aur "!" ke beech whitespace ki jaankari kho deta hai, SentencePiece use preserve karta hai.

Tokenizer pipeline ke chaar steps

Tokenization ek single operation nahi hai — ye ek poori processing pipeline hai, jiske aam taur par chaar steps hote hain:

  1. Normalization: Raw string ko "cleaner" banane wale operations — whitespace strip karna, accented characters hatana, Unicode normalization (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD jaise schemes se ek hi character ko likhne ke alag tareekon ko standard form me badalna), aur lowercasing.
  2. Pretokenization: Text ko chhoti objects me todna jo final tokens ki upper bound deti hain — aam taur par words. English, German aur kai Indo-European languages me strings ko whitespace aur punctuation par split kiya ja sakta hai. Lekin Chinese, Japanese ya Korean me words me group karna nondeterministic ho sakta hai.
  3. Tokenizer model: Pretokenized words par subword splitting model apply hota hai — BPE, Unigram ya WordPiece. Iska kaam words ko subwords me tod kar vocabulary ko chhota rakhna aur out-of-vocabulary tokens ko kam karna hai. Is step ke baad tokens ki list integers (input IDs) ki list ban jaati hai.
  4. Postprocessing: Token indices ki list par additional transformations — jaise sequence ki shuruaat ya end me special tokens add karna. BERT-style tokenizer [CLS] aur [SEP] add karta hai; SentencePiece <s> aur </s> add karta hai.
Yaad rakho: XLM-R = RoBERTa training + 100 bhashaon ka 2.5 TB corpus + SentencePiece tokenizer. 250,000 tokens ki vocabulary aur whitespace ko preserve karna hi ise multilingual banata hai.

04.3Chapter 4 · Multilingual Named Entity Recognition

Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning

Ab dekhte hain ki German par train kiya gaya model bina kisi French, Italian ya English labeled data ke un bhashaon par kaisa perform karta hai — yehi zero-shot cross-lingual transfer hai.

German par fine-tuning

Pehli strategy hai base model ko German PAN-X subset par fine-tune karna, phir uski zero-shot performance ko French, Italian aur English par evaluate karna. TrainingArguments me 3 epochs, batch size 24 aur weight decay 0.01 hain. Metrics ke liye seqeval ka F1-score use hota hai — ek prediction tabhi correct maani jaati hai jab entity ke saare words sahi predict hon. Training ke results: epoch 1 par F1 0.823, epoch 2 par 0.853, epoch 3 par 0.865. Ye NER model ke liye kaafi achhe scores hain.

Zero-shot transfer ke numbers

German test set par F1-score 0.868 aata hai. Ab wahi model, bina kisi aur training ke, doosri bhashaon par test karte hain: French par 0.714, Italian par 0.692, aur English par 0.589. French par lagbhag 15 points ki girawat aati hai — lekin model ne ek bhi labeled French example nahi dekha hai. Drop ka size bhashaon ki "doori" se juda hota hai: German (Germanic) aur French (Romance) alag families se hain, Italian bhi Romance hai isliye similar result milta hai, aur hairani ki baat ye hai ki English (Germanic) par model sabse kharab hai — intuition hamesha sahi nahi hoti.

Error analysis: model kahan galat hai

Error analysis ke liye Chapter 2 wali technique yahan bhi use hoti hai — validation examples ko loss ke hisaab se sort karna — lekin ab loss har token ke liye calculate hota hai. Whitespace token ka total loss sabse zyada hai, lekin wo sabse common bhi hai aur uska mean loss bahut kam hai. "In", "von", "der" aur "und" jaise words aksar named entities ke saath aate hain aur kabhi unka hissa bhi hote hain, isliye model unhe mix kar deta hai. Parentheses, slashes aur capital letters ka average loss relatively high hai. B-ORG ka average loss sabse zyada hai (0.66) — organization ki shuruaat sabse mushkil hai — aur confusion matrix me B-ORG aksar I-ORG se confuse hota hai.

Silver standard labels ki problem

Sabse zyada loss wale sequences me kuch labels hi galat hain — jaise ek organization ka naam person ke roop me label hai. PAN-X ki annotations ek automated process se generate hui thi — aisi annotations ko "silver standard" kehte hain, human-generated "gold standard" ke mukable — isliye aise failures expected hain. Wikipedia titles me parentheses me aksar explanation hoti hai, aur automatic annotation ne use entity ka hissa bana diya. Real use case me hum dataset clean karke, dobara train karke aur errors analyze karke iterate karte.

Zero-shot transfer kab samajhdaari hai?

Sirf 250 French examples par fine-tune karne se F1 sirf 0.137 aata hai — German se zero-shot transfer (0.714) se bahut peeche. Size badhane par (500, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000 examples) performance badhti hai, aur lagbhag 750 examples tak zero-shot transfer competitive rehta hai; uske baad French fine-tuning German wale level tak pahunch jaata hai. NER me sau documents label karwana bhi mehenga hota hai, kyunki labeling fine-grained aur time-consuming hai.

Multiple languages par ek saath fine-tuning

German aur French corpora ko concatenate_datasets() se jod kar train karne par: German 0.866, French 0.868 (German ke barabar), Italian 0.815 aur English 0.677 — unseen languages par bhi lagbhag 10 points ka improvement. Chaaron bhashaon par ek saath train karne par final comparison: sirf German par train karo to de 0.868, fr 0.714, it 0.692, en 0.589; har bhasha par alag se train karo to de 0.868, fr 0.851, it 0.819, en 0.707; saari par ek saath train karo to de 0.868, fr 0.865, it 0.858, en 0.787. Conclusion: multilingual learning se significant gains milte hain, khaas taur par jab languages similar families se hon.

Yaad rakho: Zero-shot transfer tab tak jeetta hai jab tak target language ke lagbhag 750 labeled examples na hon. Aur ek bhasha ka data add karne se unseen bhashaon par bhi performance badhti hai — multilingual training ka fayda sirf trained languages tak limited nahi hai.

def train_on_subset(dataset, num_samples):
    train_ds = dataset["train"].shuffle(seed=42).select(range(num_samples))
    valid_ds = dataset["validation"]
    test_ds = dataset["test"]
    training_args.logging_steps = len(train_ds) // batch_size
    
    trainer = Trainer(model_init=model_init, args=training_args,
        data_collator=data_collator, compute_metrics=compute_metrics,
        train_dataset=train_ds, eval_dataset=valid_ds, tokenizer=xlmr_tokenizer)
    trainer.train()
    if training_args.push_to_hub:
        trainer.push_to_hub(commit_message="Training completed!")
    
    f1_score = get_f1_score(trainer, test_ds)
    return pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
        {"num_samples": [len(train_ds)], "f1_score": [f1_score]})

from datasets import concatenate_datasets

def concatenate_splits(corpora):
    multi_corpus = DatasetDict()
    for split in corpora[0].keys():
        multi_corpus[split] = concatenate_datasets(
            [corpus[split] for corpus in corpora]).shuffle(seed=42)
    return multi_corpus

05Chapter 5 · Text Generation

Text Generation

Ab tak humne transformers ko mostly samajhne wale (NLU) tasks ke liye use kiya — classification, NER, question answering. Text generation bilkul alag duniya hai: yahan model ko naya text likhna hota hai, ek token ek baar me. Is chapter me hum GPT-2 ke through samajhte hain ki language model text kaise generate karta hai, aur decoding strategy se output ki quality kaise badalti hai.

Autoregressive language model kaise kaam karta hai

GPT-2 ek autoregressive ya causal language model hai. Iska matlab hai ki ye ek sequence ke aane ki probability estimate karta hai — prompt ke baad kaunsa token aayega, phir uske baad kaunsa, aur aise hi aage. Probability ke chain rule se poori sequence ki probability ko chhote-chhote conditional probabilities ke product me toda ja sakta hai: har token ki probability sirf usse pehle wale tokens par depend karti hai. Isi liye is task ko next token prediction kehte hain. Ye BERT se bilkul alag hai, kyunki BERT masked token predict karne ke liye aage aur peeche dono taraf ka context use karta hai, jabki GPT-2 sirf pehle wale words ko dekhta hai.

Generation ka step-by-step process

Text generate karne ke liye hum ek prompt se shuru karte hain, jaise "Transformers are the". Model prompt ke baad sabse likely next token predict karta hai, use prompt me jod deta hai, aur phir naye input se agla token predict karta hai. Ye process tab tak chalta hai jab tak end-of-sequence token na aa jaye ya maximum length poori na ho jaye. Kyunki output prompt par conditioned hota hai, is type ko conditional text generation kehte hain.

Har step par model ka language modeling head vocabulary ke har token ke liye ek logit deta hai. Softmax lagane se humein next token par ek probability distribution milti hai. Decoding method ka kaam hai is distribution se decide karna ki kaunsa token chuna jaye. Sabse likely poori sequence dhoondhna theoretically possible hai, lekin practically har possible sequence ko evaluate karna namumkin hai — isliye hum approximations use karte hain.

Text generation ki do badi challenges

  • Compute cost: Classification me ek forward pass kaafi hota hai, lekin generation me har token ke liye kam se kam ek forward pass chahiye. Beam search jaise methods me to usse bhi zyada. Isliye text generation computationally bahut mehenga hai aur scale par chalane ke liye sahi infrastructure chahiye.
  • Quality aur diversity: Generated text kitna coherent aur kitna diverse hoga, ye decoding method aur uske hyperparameters par depend karta hai. Galat decoding se repetitive ya bekaar text bhi aa sakta hai.

Book me 1.5-billion-parameter wala GPT-2 (gpt2-xl) use kiya gaya hai. Agar memory kam ho to chhota version (gpt2) bhi use kar sakte ho. Transformers library me generate() function ye saara kaam sambhalti hai — tumhe sirf prompt, maximum length aur decoding options dene hote hain.

Yaad rakho: Text generation = next token prediction, ek token ek baar me, jab tak end-of-sequence token ya max length na aa jaye. Decoding method hi decide karti hai ki output kitna achha hoga.

05.1Chapter 5 · Text Generation

Decoding Strategies — Greedy aur Beam Search

Decoding ka matlab hai model ki probability distribution ko discrete tokens me badalna. Sabse simple tareeka greedy search hai, aur uska smarter version beam search hai. Dono deterministic methods hain — inme randomness nahi hoti.

Greedy search

Greedy search har timestep par sabse zyada probability wala token chun leta hai. Book ke example me prompt "Transformers are the" se greedy decoding ne ye sentence banayi: "Transformers are the most popular toy line in the world". Har step par model top 5 choices bhi dikhata hai — jaise pehle step par "most" (8.53%), "only" (4.96%), "best" (4.65%) — lekin greedy hamesha pehli choice hi leta hai.

Greedy ki sabse badi problem hai repetition. Ek lambe prompt par (ek unicorn wali kahani) greedy output me wahi sentences baar-baar repeat hone lage. Iski wajah ye hai ki greedy sirf aaj ka best token dekhta hai, poori sequence ki overall probability nahi. Aisa ho sakta hai ki ek high-probability sequence ek low-probability word se shuru ho — greedy use kabhi dhoondh hi nahi payega. Phir bhi greedy useful hai jahan deterministic aur factually sahi short output chahiye, jaise arithmetic ("5 + 8 => 13").

Beam search

Beam search har step par sirf ek token nahi, balki top-b sabse likely tokens (beams) ko track karta hai, jahan b ko number of beams kehte hain. Har step par saare beams ke possible extensions me se b sabse likely extensions chune jate hain. Process tab tak chalta hai jab tak max length ya end-of-sequence token na aa jaye, aur ant me b beams ko unki log probabilities se rank karke sabse likely sequence chuni jati hai. generate() me beam search ke liye bas num_beams=5 pass karna hota hai.

Probabilities ki jagah log probabilities kyun?

Sequence ki overall probability bahut saari chhoti probabilities ka product hoti hai. Agar sequence 1024 tokens ki ho aur har token ki probability 0.5 ho, to overall probability 0.5^1024 hoti hai — lagbhag 5.56e-309 — jo computer ke liye represent karna mushkil hai aur underflow ho jata hai. Log lene se product, sum me badal jata hai: log probability lagbhag -709.78 hoti hai, jo aaram se handle ho jati hai. Isliye sequences ko compare karne ke liye log probabilities use hoti hain — higher (kam negative) behtar hoti hai.

Book ke numbers se comparison

Unicorn wale prompt par greedy decoding ki sequence log-probability -87.43 thi, jabki beam search (5 beams) ki -55.23 thi — matlab beam search ne zyada likely sequence dhoondhi. Lekin beam search me bhi repetition thi. Iske liye no_repeat_ngram_size=2 parameter use kiya gaya, jo kisi bhi 2-gram ko dobara aane se rokta hai — uski probability ko zero kar deta hai. Isse repetition ruk gaya aur text coherent raha, halanki log-probability -93.12 ho gayi. Ye ek trade-off hai: repetition rokne se score gir sakta hai, lekin text padhne me behtar lagta hai.

Beam search with n-gram penalty summarization aur machine translation jaise tasks me bahut use hota hai, jahan factual correctness important hoti hai. Jahan diversity zyada important ho — jaise open-domain chitchat ya story generation — wahan sampling behtar hoti hai.

Yaad rakho: Greedy har step ka best token leta hai aur repeat kar sakta hai; beam search b parallel hypotheses track karke zyada likely sequence dhoondhta hai. Log probabilities underflow se bachati hain, aur n-gram penalty repetition rokti hai.

# hide_output
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
model_name = "gpt2-xl"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/05_text-generation.ipynb)
# hide_output
import pandas as pd

input_txt = "Transformers are the"
input_ids = tokenizer(input_txt, return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"].to(device)
iterations = []
n_steps = 8
choices_per_step = 5

with torch.no_grad():
    for _ in range(n_steps):
        iteration = dict()
        iteration["Input"] = tokenizer.decode(input_ids[0])
        output = model(input_ids=input_ids)
        # Select logits of the first batch and the last token and apply softmax
        next_token_logits = output.logits[0, -1, :]
        next_token_probs = torch.softmax(next_token_logits, dim=-1)
        sorted_ids = torch.argsort(next_token_probs, dim=-1, descending=True)
        # Store tokens with highest probabilities
        for choice_idx in range(choices_per_step):
            token_id = sorted_ids[choice_idx]
            token_prob = next_token_probs[token_id].cpu().numpy()
            token_choice = (
                f"{tokenizer.decode(token_id)} ({100 * token_prob:.2f}%)"
            )
            iteration[f"Choice {choice_idx+1}"] = token_choice
        # Append predicted next token to input
        input_ids = torch.cat([input_ids, sorted_ids[None, 0, None]], dim=-1)
        iterations.append(iteration)
        
pd.DataFrame(iterations)

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/05_text-generation.ipynb)
import torch.nn.functional as F

def log_probs_from_logits(logits, labels):
    logp = F.log_softmax(logits, dim=-1)
    logp_label = torch.gather(logp, 2, labels.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(-1)
    return logp_label
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/05_text-generation.ipynb)
def sequence_logprob(model, labels, input_len=0):
    with torch.no_grad():
        output = model(labels)
        log_probs = log_probs_from_logits(
            output.logits[:, :-1, :], labels[:, 1:])
        seq_log_prob = torch.sum(log_probs[:, input_len:])
    return seq_log_prob.cpu().numpy()

print(tokenizer.decode(output_greedy[0]))
print(f"\nlog-prob: {logp:.2f}")

05.2Chapter 5 · Text Generation

Sampling — Top-k aur Top-p

Deterministic decoding ke opposite hai sampling — probability distribution se randomly token chunna. Sampling se text me diversity aur creativity aati hai, lekin control karna padta hai warna output gibberish ban jata hai. Temperature, top-k aur top-p — ye teen knobs hain jinse tum is trade-off ko control karte ho.

Temperature

Sampling ka sabse simple tareeka hai har timestep par poori vocabulary ki distribution se randomly sample karna. Temperature parameter T logits ko softmax se pehle rescale karta hai. Jab T bahut chhota hota hai (T << 1), to distribution ek jagah peak ho jati hai aur rare tokens dab jate hain — output zyada predictable aur coherent hota hai. Jab T bahut bada hota hai (T >> 1), to distribution flat ho jati hai aur har token lagbhag equally likely ban jata hai.

Book ke experiment me temperature 2.0 par output lagbhag gibberish tha — ajeeb grammar aur banaye hue words. Temperature 0.5 par output kaafi coherent tha, aur ek quote bhi aa gaya. Lesson ye hai: temperature se quality control hoti hai, lekin hamesha coherence (low temperature) aur diversity (high temperature) ke beech trade-off hota hai, jo use case ke hisaab se tune karna padta hai.

Top-k sampling

Ek badi problem ye hai ki poori vocabulary se sample karne par kabhi-kabhi bahut unlikely token bhi chun liya jata hai. GPT-2 ki vocabulary me 50,257 tokens hain. Book ke analysis me dikhaya gaya ki top 1,000 tokens ko chunne ki probability lagbhag 96% hai — matlab 100 me se 1 baar top 1,000 ke bahar ka token aa sakta hai. Ek token ke liye ye chhota lagta hai, lekin jab tum sau baar sample karte ho, to ek unlikely token aa hi jata hai, aur wo poori generation ko bigaad sakta hai.

Top-k sampling iska solution hai: sirf k sabse zyada probability wale tokens me se sample karo. generate() me top_k=50 ka matlab hai har step par sirf top 50 tokens ka pool. Book me top_k=50 se arguably sabse human-like text bana. Lekin k ko manually choose karna padta hai, aur ye har step par same rehta hai — chahe distribution peaked ho ya flat.

Top-p (nucleus) sampling

Top-p, jise nucleus sampling bhi kehte hain, ek dynamic cutoff use karta hai. Fixed k ki jagah hum ek probability mass set karte hain, jaise 95% ya 90%. Tokens ko probability ke descending order me sort karke ek-ek karke joda jata hai jab tak unki probabilities ka sum p tak na pahunch jaye. Agar distribution peaked hai to sirf ek token kaafi ho sakta hai; agar flat hai to sau tokens bhi aa sakte hain. generate() me top_p=0.90 se coherent story bani, jisme migration ke baare me ek naya twist bhi tha.

Dono ko combine bhi kar sakte ho: top_k=50 aur top_p=0.9 ka matlab hai zyada se zyada 50 tokens ke pool me se 90% probability mass wale tokens. Aur beam search ko sampling ke saath bhi use kar sakte ho — greedy ki jagah sampled tokens se beams banaye jate hain.

Kaunsa decoding method best hai?

Koi universal best method nahi hai. Agar precise kaam hai — arithmetic ya kisi specific sawaal ka jawab — to low temperature ya greedy + beam search use karo taaki sabse likely answer mile. Agar lamba, creative text chahiye to sampling use karo, temperature badhao ya top-k aur top-p ka mix use karo. Best strategy dhoondhne ke liye experimentation aur subjective evaluation chahiye — aur ideally ek metric, jo agle section me aayega.

Yaad rakho: Temperature distribution ko sharp ya flat karta hai; top-k fixed pool deta hai; top-p probability mass ke hisaab se dynamic pool deta hai. Coherence chahiye to deterministic, creativity chahiye to sampling.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

def softmax(logits, T=1):
    e_x = np.exp(logits / T)
    return e_x / e_x.sum()

logits = np.exp(np.random.random(1000))
sorted_logits = np.sort(logits)[::-1]
x = np.arange(1000)

for T in [0.5, 1.0, 2.0]:
    plt.step(x, softmax(sorted_logits, T), label=f"T={T}")
plt.legend(loc="best")
plt.xlabel("Sorted token probabilities")
plt.ylabel("Probability")
plt.show()

05.3Chapter 5 · Text Generation

Metrics — Perplexity

Decoding method chunne ke baad sawal ye hai: model achha hai ya nahi, ye measure kaise karein? Classification me accuracy kaam karti hai, lekin generated text ke liye ek alag metric chahiye. Language models ke liye sabse classic metric hai perplexity.

Perplexity kya hai

Perplexity measure karti hai ki language model kisi text ko dekh kar kitna "surprised" hota hai. Mathematically ye average negative log-likelihood ka exponent hoti hai: model jitni zyada probability sahi next token ko deta hai, utni kam perplexity hoti hai. Simple shabdon me — perplexity batati hai ki model ko har jagah par average kitne tokens ke beech choose karna pad raha hai. Agar perplexity 10 hai, to model har step par lagbhag 10 options me confuse hai; agar 100 hai, to confusion bahut zyada hai. Isliye lower perplexity behtar hoti hai.

Perplexity kaise use hoti hai

Perplexity ko ek held-out test set par compute kiya jata hai — aisa text jo training me nahi tha. Do language models ko compare karne ke liye dono ki perplexity same test set par measure karo; jiski kam hogi, wo text ko behtar predict kar raha hai. Ye pretraining ke dauraan progress track karne ke liye bhi use hoti hai: jaise-jaise training aage badhti hai, perplexity girni chahiye. Book me jo sequence log-probability ka concept aaya tha (greedy -87.43, beam -55.23), perplexity usi idea se judi hai — dono hi model ki di hui probabilities se banti hain, bas perplexity ko per-token average aur exponent ke saath normalize kiya jata hai taaki alag length ke texts compare ho sakein.

Perplexity ki limitations

  • Ye sirf prediction measure karti hai, generation quality nahi: Kam perplexity wala model bhi repetitive ya factually galat text generate kar sakta hai. Decoding strategy ka asar perplexity me dikhai nahi deta.
  • Same data par hi compare karo: Alag test sets ya alag tokenizers par perplexity compare karna misleading hota hai, kyunki vocabulary size aur text style se numbers badal jate hain.
  • Human judgment se match nahi karti: Ek text jo insaan ko achha lage, uski perplexity zyada bhi ho sakti hai, aur ek boring repetitive text ki perplexity kam bhi ho sakti hai.

Isi liye text generation ke liye perplexity ke saath-saath task-specific metrics bhi use hote hain. Agle chapter me hum BLEU aur ROUGE dekhenge, jo generated text ko reference text se compare karte hain — BLEU translation ke liye precision par focus karta hai, aur ROUGE summarization ke liye recall par. Aur ant me hamesha human judgment sabse behtar measure rehta hai.

Yaad rakho: Perplexity = model kitna surprised hai. Lower behtar hai, lekin ye sirf next-token prediction measure karti hai — generated text ki coherence ya factuality ka poora sach nahi batati.

06Chapter 6 · Summarization

Summarization

Summarization ka matlab hai ek lambe document ko chhota karke uske main points nikaalna. Ye kaam research article ho, financial report ho ya emails ki thread — har jagah chahiye hota hai. Lekin ye transformers ke liye mushkil task hai, kyunki isme lambe passages ko samajhna, unpar reasoning karna, aur fluent text likhna — teeno chahiye hota hai.

Extractive vs abstractive summarization

Do tareeke hain summary banane ke. Extractive summarization me original text se hi sentences chun kar jode jate hain — kuch naya likha nahi jata. Abstractive summarization me model naye sentences likhta hai jo original ke main topics ko capture karte hain. Book ka focus abstractive summarization par hai, kyunki ye zyada mushkil aur zyada useful hai.

CNN/DailyMail dataset

Is chapter ka canonical dataset hai CNN/DailyMail — lagbhag 300,000 news articles aur unke summaries ke pairs. Summaries abstractive hain, kyunki ye articles ke saath lage bullet points se bane hain, seedha excerpt nahi. Dataset me teen columns hain: article (poora news article), highlights (summary), aur id. Book me version 3.0.0 use kiya gaya hai. Ek example me article lagbhag 3,192 characters ka tha aur summary sirf 180 characters ki — matlab 17 guna ka difference. Yehi ratio summarization ki challenge dikhata hai.

Lambe documents ki problem

Zyadatar transformer models ka context size lagbhag 1,000 tokens tak limited hota hai — matlab kuch paragraphs. Lekin news articles isse bahut lambe hote hain. Standard tareeka ye hai ki text ko model ke context size se aage truncate kar diya jaye. Ye crude hai, kyunki important information document ke end me bhi ho sakti hai, lekin abhi ke architectures ke saath yahi limitation accept karni padti hai. Lambe documents ko summarize karna aaj bhi ek open research problem hai — ek approach ye hai ki document ko recursively summarize kiya jaye, chhote parts se shuru karke.

Ek simple baseline

News articles ko summarize karne ka ek common baseline hai article ke pehle teen sentences lena. NLTK ke sentence tokenizer se ye aasani se implement ho jata hai. Ye baseline hairan karne wali baat hai — aage chal kar dekhenge ki ye simple tareeka bhi transformer models se zyada peeche nahi rehta. Iska reason ye hai ki news articles me sabse important information aksar shuru me hi hoti hai. Koi bhi naya model banane se pehle aise baseline se compare karna bahut zaroori hai.

Summarization ek classic sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) task hai — input ek text hai, output ek text hai. Isi liye yahan encoder-decoder transformers sabse achhe hote hain, jo hum agle section me dekhenge.

Yaad rakho: Summarization me abstractive summary naye sentences likhta hai, extractive purane sentences chunta hai. Lambe documents aur limited context size is task ki sabse badi challenges hain.

06.1Chapter 6 · Summarization

Seq2Seq Models — BART, T5, PEGASUS

Summarization ke liye encoder-decoder (seq2seq) models sabse natural choice hain: encoder poora document padhta hai, decoder summary likhta hai. Is section me hum chaar models ko compare karte hain — GPT-2, T5, BART aur PEGASUS — ek hi news article par.

GPT-2 — TL;DR trick

GPT-2 decoder-only model hai, summarization ke liye train nahi hua. Phir bhi ek trick se use summary likhne par majboor kiya ja sakta hai: input text ke end me "TL;DR:" jod do. "TL;DR" (too long; didn't read) ka matlab hota hai lambe post ka chhota version. Book me pipeline("text-generation", model="gpt2-xl") se ye try kiya gaya. Result bekaar tha — GPT-2 ne article ko summarize karne ki jagah characters ke baare me likhna shuru kar diya aur facts invent kar diye (hallucination). Ye dikhata hai ki bina task-specific training ke model summary nahi likh sakta.

T5 — text-to-text framework

T5 har task ko text-to-text problem bana deta hai: input ek text hai, output ek text hai. Summarization ke liye input format hota hai "summarize: <ARTICLE>", aur translation ke liye "translate English to German: <TEXT>". T5 checkpoints unsupervised data (masked words reconstruct karna) aur supervised data (summarization samet kai tasks) ke mixture par train hote hain, isliye bina fine-tuning ke bhi summarize kar sakte hain. pipeline("summarization", model="t5-large") input formatting khud sambhal leta hai. Book ke example me T5 ka summary ground truth ke kaafi kareeb tha.

BART — BERT + GPT-2 ka combination

BART bhi encoder-decoder transformer hai, jo corrupted inputs ko reconstruct karne ke liye train hota hai. Ye BERT aur GPT-2 dono ki pretraining schemes ko combine karta hai. Book me facebook/bart-large-cnn checkpoint use hua hai, jo CNN/DailyMail par specifically fine-tune kiya gaya hai. Iska summary bhi ground truth ke bahut kareeb aaya — sirf ek fact galat tha (ek extra detail jod di).

PEGASUS — summarization ke liye bana pretraining objective

PEGASUS ka idea ye hai ki pretraining objective jitna downstream task ke kareeb ho, utna behtar result milega. Iska pretraining objective hai masked sentences ko predict karna: ek bade corpus me se un sentences ko chuna gaya jo apne aas-paas ke paragraph ka sabse zyada content rakhti thin, aur model ko unhe reconstruct karne ke liye train kiya gaya. Ye summarization ke bahut kareeb hai. Book me google/pegasus-cnn_dailymail use hua, aur iska output ground truth se sabse zyada milta-julta tha — lagbhag identical.

Comparison se kya seekha

GPT-2 (bina training ke) sabse kharab raha, T5 beech me, aur BART aur PEGASUS (sirf is task par fine-tune hue) sabse achhe. Lekin sirf ek example dekh kar decide nahi karna chahiye ki production me kaunsa model use karein — iske liye systematic metric chahiye, jo agle section me aayega. Ek practical note: in models me PEGASUS ka ek special newline token hota hai, isliye uske output me " .<n>" ko newline se replace karna padta hai.

Yaad rakho: T5 har task ko text-to-text banata hai, BART corrupted text reconstruct karta hai, aur PEGASUS gap-sentences predict karta hai — jo summarization ke sabse kareeb pretraining objective hai.

06.2Chapter 6 · Summarization

ROUGE Metric

Generated text ko evaluate karna mushkil hai, kyunki ek hi summary ke dozens sahi versions ho sakte hain — synonyms, paraphrases, alag wording. Exact match to bilkul kaam nahi karta. Isliye text generation ke liye do standard metrics bane: BLEU aur ROUGE.

BLEU — precision-based metric

BLEU ka idea simple hai: generated text ke kitne words ya n-grams reference text me bhi aate hain? Ye precision-based metric hai — generated text ke words me se kitne sahi hain. Ek problem hai: agar generated text ek hi word ko baar-baar repeat kare aur wo word reference me ho, to vanilla precision perfect ho jayegi. Isliye BLEU me clipped counting hoti hai — ek word utni hi baar gina jata hai jitni baar wo reference me aata hai. Example: reference "the cat is on the mat" aur prediction "the the the the the the" ho, to vanilla precision 6/6 hoti, lekin modified precision sirf 2/6 hoti hai.

BLEU n-grams tak extend hota hai — BLEU-4 me 1-gram se 4-gram tak ki modified precision ka geometric mean liya jata hai. Chhote generations ko faida na mile, isliye ek brevity penalty bhi lagti hai: agar generated text reference se chhota ho to score kam ho jata hai. BLEU ki limitations hain: ye synonyms ko nahi samajhta, aur iske steps kaafi ad hoc hain. SacreBLEU tokenization ko internalize karke is problem ko solve karta hai, isliye benchmarking ke liye wahi preferred hai.

ROUGE — recall-based metric

ROUGE summarization ke liye bana hai, jahan recall zyada important hai — matlab reference ki saari important information generated summary me aani chahiye. BLEU poochta hai "generated text me se kitna reference me hai", jabki ROUGE poochta hai "reference me se kitna generated text me hai". Aaj kal ROUGE me precision aur recall dono measure karke unka harmonic mean (F1-score) report kiya jata hai.

ROUGE ke variants hain: ROUGE-1 (unigrams), ROUGE-2 (bigrams), aur ROUGE-L jo longest common subsequence (LCS) par based hai. LCS do strings ka sabse lamba common subsequence hota hai — jaise "abab" aur "abc" ka LCS "ab" hai, length 2. Ise reference aur generated text ki length se normalize karke F-score jaisa scheme banaya jata hai. Datasets library me ROUGE-L (per-sentence average) aur ROUGE-Lsum (poore summary par) dono calculate hote hain.

Book ke results

Ek hi example par ROUGE F1 scores ye mile: baseline (pehle 3 sentences) ROUGE-1 0.30, GPT-2 0.19, T5 0.49, BART 0.58, aur PEGASUS 0.87. PEGASUS ROUGE-2 (0.66) aur ROUGE-L (0.80) par bhi sabse aage tha. Lekin ye results sirf ek sample par hain — reliable nahi. Simple baseline ka itna achha perform karna dikhata hai ki news summarization me pehle sentences me hi bahut information hoti hai.

Metrics ko code me load karna aasan hai: load_metric("rouge") ya load_metric("sacrebleu"). Metric ek aggregator ki tarah kaam karta hai — add() ya add_batch() se samples jodo, phir compute() se score nikalo. ROUGE confidence intervals bhi deta hai (by default 5th aur 95th percentile).

Yaad rakho: BLEU precision dekhta hai (translation ke liye), ROUGE recall dekhta hai (summarization ke liye). Dono hi perfect nahi hain — human judgment hamesha final measure rehta hai.

06.3Chapter 6 · Summarization

Summarization ko Evaluate Karna

Ek example par achha score dekhna kaafi nahi hai. Sahi evaluation ke liye humein chahiye: ek test set, ek metric, aur ek model — aur phir in teeno ko sahi tareeke se jodna. Is section me hum PEGASUS ko CNN/DailyMail par properly evaluate karte hain, aur phir apna khud ka summarization model train karte hain.

PEGASUS ko CNN/DailyMail par evaluate karna

Test set me lagbhag 10,000 samples hain. Har sample ke liye summary generate karna bahut slow hai — har token ke liye ek forward pass chahiye, aur beam search se ye beams se multiply ho jata hai. Isliye book me test set ko shuffle karke 1,000 samples ka subset liya gaya (seed 42), jo ek GPU par ek ghante se kam me complete ho jata hai aur stable estimate deta hai.

Evaluation me beam search use hua: num_beams=8, max_length=128, length_penalty=0.8 (taaki sequences zyada lambi na hon), aur input articles ko 1024 tokens par truncate kiya gaya. Results: baseline ka ROUGE-1 0.396, ROUGE-2 0.174, ROUGE-Lsum 0.361; PEGASUS ka ROUGE-1 0.434, ROUGE-2 0.211, ROUGE-Lsum 0.373. Ye numbers published results ke bahut kareeb hain. Ek important observation: loss aur per-token accuracy ROUGE se decoupled hote hain — loss decoding strategy se independent hota hai, jabki ROUGE us par strongly depend karta hai. Isliye decoding strategy ko carefully choose karna chahiye.

Apna model train karna — SAMSum dataset

Ab hum dialogues ko summarize karne ke liye apna model train karte hain. SAMSum dataset me chat dialogues aur unke brief summaries hain — jaise customer support ki baat-cheet. Isme 14,732 training, 819 validation aur 818 test examples hain. Dialogues mostly 100–200 tokens ke hote hain aur summaries lagbhag 20–40 tokens ki — ek tweet ke barabar. CNN/DailyMail par train hua PEGASUS is par kharab perform karta hai (ROUGE-1 sirf 0.296), kyunki domain bilkul alag hai — dialogue ki language informal hoti hai aur summaries zyada abstract hote hain.

Training ke key concepts

  • Teacher forcing: Decoder ko labels ko ek position shift karke input diya jata hai, taaki next token predict karte waqt use sirf pehle wale ground truth tokens dikhein, current ya future wale nahi.
  • DataCollatorForSeq2Seq: Ye collator shifting aur padding ko sambhalta hai — padding tokens ko loss me ignore karne ke liye unhe -100 set kar deta hai.
  • Gradient accumulation: Model bada hai isliye batch size 1 rakhni padi. Chhota batch convergence kharab karta hai, isliye 16 chhote batches ke gradients accumulate karke ek optimization step liya gaya. Ye slow hai lekin GPU memory bachata hai.
  • Target tokenizer: Kuch models ko decoder inputs ke liye special tokens chahiye hote hain, isliye summary tokenize karte waqt tokenizer.as_target_tokenizer() context use hota hai.

Ek epoch fine-tuning ke baad ROUGE-1 0.296 se badh kar 0.428 ho gaya, ROUGE-2 0.088 se 0.201, aur ROUGE-Lsum 0.230 se 0.341. Model ne seekh liya ki dialogue ko extract karne ki jagah synthesize karna hai — jaise ek custom dialogue par usne sahi summary banayi ki kaun log mil kar kya karne wale hain. Training ke dauraan generations evaluate karne ke liye Seq2SeqTrainingArguments me predict_with_generate=True aur Seq2SeqTrainer use kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: Evaluation se pehle baseline banao, phir bade test set par metric se compare karo. Domain badalne par fine-tuning zaroori hai — CNN/DailyMail wala model dialogues par fail hota hai.

def evaluate_summaries_baseline(dataset, metric,
                                column_text="article", 
                                column_summary="highlights"):
    summaries = [three_sentence_summary(text) for text in dataset[column_text]]
    metric.add_batch(predictions=summaries,
                     references=dataset[column_summary])    
    score = metric.compute()
    return score

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/06_summarization.ipynb)
from tqdm import tqdm
import torch

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

def chunks(list_of_elements, batch_size):
    """Yield successive batch-sized chunks from list_of_elements."""
    for i in range(0, len(list_of_elements), batch_size):
        yield list_of_elements[i : i + batch_size]

def evaluate_summaries_pegasus(dataset, metric, model, tokenizer, 
                               batch_size=16, device=device, 
                               column_text="article", 
                               column_summary="highlights"):
    article_batches = list(chunks(dataset[column_text], batch_size))
    target_batches = list(chunks(dataset[column_summary], batch_size))

    for article_batch, target_batch in tqdm(
        zip(article_batches, target_batches), total=len(article_batches)):
        
        inputs = tokenizer(article_batch, max_length=1024,  truncation=True, 
                        padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt")
        
        summaries = model.generate(input_ids=inputs["input_ids"].to(device),
                         attention_mask=inputs["attention_mask"].to(device), 
                         length_penalty=0.8, num_beams=8, max_length=128)
        
        decoded_summaries = [tokenizer.decode(s, skip_special_tokens=True, 
                                clean_up_tokenization_spaces=True) 
               for s in summaries]
        decoded_summaries = [d.replace("<n>", " ") for d in decoded_summaries]
        metric.add_batch(predictions=decoded_summaries, references=target_batch)
        
    score = metric.compute()
    return score

def convert_examples_to_features(example_batch):
    input_encodings = tokenizer(example_batch["dialogue"], max_length=1024,
                                truncation=True)
    
    with tokenizer.as_target_tokenizer():
        target_encodings = tokenizer(example_batch["summary"], max_length=128,
                                     truncation=True)
    
    return {"input_ids": input_encodings["input_ids"],
            "attention_mask": input_encodings["attention_mask"],
            "labels": target_encodings["input_ids"]}

dataset_samsum_pt = dataset_samsum.map(convert_examples_to_features, 
                                       batched=True)
columns = ["input_ids", "labels", "attention_mask"]
dataset_samsum_pt.set_format(type="torch", columns=columns)

07Chapter 7 · Question Answering

Question Answering

Google par sawaal poochho to wo sirf links nahi deta — wo seedha answer snippet bhi dikhata hai. Iske peeche hai question answering (QA). Is chapter me hum ek ecommerce use case banate hain: customer reviews se product ke baare me poochhe gaye sawaalon ke jawab nikaalna.

Extractive QA kya hai

QA ke kai flavors hain, lekin sabse common hai extractive QA — jahan jawab ek document ke andar ek text span ke roop me milta hai. Document ek web page, legal contract ya news article ho sakta hai. Process do stages ka hota hai: pehle relevant documents retrieve karo, phir unme se answer extract karo. Yehi two-stage process modern QA systems, semantic search engines aur intelligent assistants ki buniyaad hai.

QA ke aur types bhi hain: community QA (forums par users ke likhe question-answer pairs me se closest answer dhoondhna), long-form QA (khule sawaalon ke paragraph-lambey jawab generate karna), aur tables par QA (jahan model aggregation bhi kar sakta hai).

Use case — reviews se jawab

Online shopping me customer reviews se specific sawaalon ke jawab mil sakte hain — jaise "Kya ye guitar strap ke saath aata hai?" ya "Kya ye camera raat me use ho sakta hai?" — jo product description se nahi milte. Lekin popular products ke sau ya hazaaron reviews hote hain, unme dhoondhna mushkil hai. Community QA platforms par jawab milne me din lag jate hain. Isliye hum transformers se ek aisa system banate hain jo turant jawab de.

Closed-domain vs open-domain

QA systems ko unke data ke domain se categorize kiya jata hai. Closed-domain QA ek narrow topic ke baare me hota hai — jaise ek hi product category — jabki open-domain QA lagbhag kisi bhi cheez ke baare me hota hai, jaise poora product catalog. Closed-domain me kam documents search karne padte hain, isliye ye aasan hota hai. Is chapter me hum closed-domain (electronics products) par focus karte hain, lekin techniques open-domain me bhi generalize hoti hain.

SubjQA dataset

Book me SubjQA dataset use hua hai — 10,000 se zyada customer reviews, chhe domains me: TripAdvisor, Restaurants, Movies, Books, Electronics aur Grocery. Har review ke saath ek question hai jiska jawab review ki ek ya zyada sentences me milta hai. Is dataset ki khaas baat ye hai ki zyadatar questions aur answers subjective hain — matlab wo users ke personal experience par depend karte hain. Jaise "poor quality" ka matlab har user ke liye alag ho sakta hai, aur query ke important parts review me dikhte hi nahi. Isliye keyword search se ye answer nahi mil sakta.

Electronics subset me train me 1,295, test me 358 aur validation me 255 questions hain — kul 1,908. Dataset chhota hai, jo real-world jaisa hai, kyunki extractive QA data ko label karna mehenga aur time-consuming hota hai — domain experts chahiye hote hain. Kuch questions unanswerable bhi hain — jinka jawab review me hai hi nahi — aur model ko ye bhi pehchanana chahiye.

Yaad rakho: Extractive QA = relevant document retrieve karo + usme se answer span extract karo. Subjective questions (jaise reviews wale) factual questions se zyada mushkil hote hain.

07.1Chapter 7 · Question Answering

SQuAD aur Span Extraction

Answer span extract karne ka standard tareeka hai span classification — model ko answer ke start aur end token predict karne hote hain. Iska foundation hai SQuAD dataset, jo extractive QA ka sabse famous benchmark hai.

SQuAD dataset

SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset) Wikipedia articles se banaya gaya: articles ko paragraphs me baanta gaya, aur crowdworkers se har paragraph ke liye questions aur answers likhwaye gaye. Pehle version me har question ka answer passage me zaroor hota tha. Lekin jald hi models humans se behtar perform karne lage, to SQuAD 2.0 banaya gaya — isme adversarial questions jode gaye jo passage se related to hain lekin unka jawab text se nahi mil sakta. Iske baad bhi models ka superhuman performance genuine reading comprehension nahi dikhata — unanswerable questions aksar passage ke patterns (jaise antonyms) se pehchane ja sakte hain. Isliye ek aur dataset banaya gaya jisme real users ke search questions hain aur answers zyada lambe hote hain.

Span classification kaise kaam karta hai

QA head ek linear layer hoti hai jo encoder ke hidden states se har token ke liye do logits compute karti hai: ek start token ke liye, ek end token ke liye. Matlab QA ek tarah ka token classification hai, jaise NER. Training set chhota ho (SubjQA me sirf 1,295 examples) to behtar hai ki SQuAD jaise bade dataset par pehle se fine-tune hue model se shuru karo — aise models ki reading comprehension strong hoti hai. Book me MiniLM use hua hai — BERT-base ka distilled version jo 99% performance preserve karke do guna fast hai, SQuAD 2.0 par F1-score 79.5 ke saath. Checkpoint hai deepset/minilm-uncased-squad2.

QA ke liye tokenization

Input (question, context) pair ke roop me diya jata hai aur format hota hai: [CLS] question tokens [SEP] context tokens [SEP]. token_type_ids batata hai kaunsa token question ka hai (0) aur kaunsa context ka (1). Example: question "How much music can this hold?" aur context "An MP3 is about 1 MB/minute, so about 6000 hours depending on file size." par model ne sahi answer "6000 hours" extract kiya — start aur end logits ka argmax lekar, phir us span ko decode karke.

Pipeline aur unanswerable questions

Transformers me ye sab pipeline("question-answering") me wrapped hai. Ye answer ke saath score bhi deta hai (logits par softmax se), aur topk=3 se multiple answers bhi de sakta hai. Unanswerable questions ke liye model [CLS] token ko high start aur end score deta hai, aur pipeline use empty string me map kar deta hai (jab handle_impossible_answer=True ho). Simple argmax kabhi-kabhi question ke tokens ko bhi answer bana sakta hai, isliye pipeline constraints lagati hai — jaise start index end se pehle hona chahiye aur answer context ke andar hona chahiye.

Lambe passages — sliding window

Context aksar model ki maximum sequence length (MiniLM ke liye 512 tokens) se zyada lamba hota hai. Classification me hum text truncate kar dete hain, lekin QA me answer passage ke end me bhi ho sakta hai, isliye truncation kaam nahi karega. Solution hai sliding window: inputs par ek window slide karke multiple question-context pairs banaye jate hain. Tokenizer me return_overflowing_tokens=True se ye enable hota hai, window size max_length se aur stride doc_stride se control hoti hai. Overlapping windows se answer kisi bhi window me mil sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: QA = span classification. Model har token ke liye start aur end logits deta hai; SQuAD par fine-tune hua model achha starting point hai; lambe context ke liye sliding window use karo.

07.2Chapter 7 · Question Answering

Retrieval with Haystack

Sirf question dene se kaam nahi chalta — system ko khud relevant reviews dhoondhne hote hain. Iske liye modern QA systems retriever-reader architecture use karte hain. Is section me hum Haystack library se aisa pipeline banate hain.

Retriever-reader architecture

System ke do main components hote hain. Retriever query ke liye relevant documents dhoondhta hai, aur Reader un documents se answer extract karta hai. Retriever do tarah ke hote hain: sparse retrievers word frequencies se document aur query ko sparse vectors ke roop me represent karte hain (jaise TF-IDF ya BM25), jabki dense retrievers transformers se contextualized embeddings banate hain jo semantic meaning capture karte hain. Dense retrievers us waqt behtar hote hain jab query ke words review ke words se exactly match na karein.

Iske alawa do aur components hote hain: Document store (ek document-oriented database jo documents aur metadata store karta hai) aur Pipeline (saare components ko ek graph me jodta hai taaki custom query flows ban sakein).

BM25 sparse retriever

BM25 TF-IDF ka improved version hai. Ye term frequency ko jaldi saturate karta hai aur document length ko normalize karta hai taaki chhote documents ko faida mile. Book me Elasticsearch document store use hua hai, jo sparse aur dense dono retrievers ke saath compatible hai. Reviews ko document store me load kiya gaya — kul 1,615 unique documents — har document ke saath metadata me product ID aur question ID rakhe gaye taaki query ko ek hi product tak filter kiya ja sake. Ye bahut important hai: bina product filter ke "camera quality kaisi hai?" par phone ke reviews bhi aa sakte hain jabki user laptop camera ke baare me pooch raha ho.

Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR)

DPR state-of-the-art dense retriever hai. Isme do BERT encoders hote hain — ek question ke liye, ek passage ke liye — jo input text ko [CLS] token ke d-dimensional vector me map karte hain. Encoders ko relevant (positive) aur irrelevant (negative) passages ke saath train kiya jata hai taaki relevant question-passage pairs ki similarity zyada ho. Book me NQ corpus par fine-tune hue encoders use hue. Dense retriever banane ke baad saare indexed documents par encoders chala kar unki embeddings update karni padti hain.

Reader aur end-to-end pipeline

Reader ke liye book me FARMReader use hua hai (MiniLM checkpoint ke saath). Transformers ke QA pipeline se iske do differences hain: FARM logits ko normalize nahi karta, isliye alag passages ke answers ko aasani se compare kar sakte ho; aur ye overlapping windows se aaye duplicate answers ko hata deta hai. Sliding window yahan max_seq_len=384 aur doc_stride=128 se control hoti hai. Dono components ExtractiveQAPipeline me jude — query, top_k_retriever aur top_k_reader pass karo, aur system top answers unke review snippets ke saath de deta hai.

Yaad rakho: Retriever relevant documents dhoondhta hai, reader answer extract karta hai. Retriever poore system ki performance ki upper bound set karta hai — agar retriever sahi document nahi laaya to reader kuch nahi kar sakta. IMPORTANT: Book me jo Haystack aur search engine versions use hue hain wo 2022 ke hain aur ab outdated hain — runnable code ke liye hamesha current Haystack docs follow karo, book ke version numbers ko current mat samjho.

07.3Chapter 7 · Question Answering

QA System End-to-End

Pipeline ban gaya, lekin ye achha hai ya nahi — ye measure karna hoga. Is section me hum retriever aur reader ko alag-alag evaluate karte hain, domain adaptation se performance badhate hain, aur generative QA tak jate hain.

Retriever ko evaluate karna — recall

Retriever ka common metric hai recall: kul relevant documents me se kitne retrieve hue. Yahan "relevant" ka matlab hai ki answer passage me maujood hai ya nahi. Book me BM25 ka Recall@3 0.95 mila — matlab 95% questions ke liye sahi document top 3 me aa gaya. k badhane se recall badhta hai, lekin reader ko zyada documents milte hain aur latency badhti hai. Plot me k=5 ke aas-paas inflection point tha aur k=10 se recall lagbhag perfect ho gaya. DPR se chhote k par koi boost nahi mila — recall k=3 ke aas-paas saturate ho gaya. Ek complementary metric hai mean average precision (mAP), jo sahi answers ko ranking me upar rakhne par reward deta hai.

Reader ko evaluate karna — EM aur F1

Reader ke do main metrics hain. Exact Match (EM) binary hai: predicted aur ground truth answer ke characters exactly match hon to 1, warna 0. F1-score precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai, token level par compute hota hai. Example: prediction "about 6000 hours" aur label "6000 hours" par EM 0 hai lekin F1 0.8 hai — EM zyada strict hai. Lekin F1 bhi dhokha de sakta hai: galat prediction "about 6000 dollars" par bhi F1 0.4 mil jata hai. Isliye dono metrics ko saath me track karna chahiye.

Domain adaptation — sabse bada gain

SQuAD par fine-tune hua MiniLM SubjQA par bahut kharab perform karta hai (SQuAD 2.0 par EM 76.1 aur F1 79.5 ke mukable), kyunki reviews ki language Wikipedia se bilkul alag aur informal hai, aur questions subjective hain. Solution hai domain adaptation: model ko SubjQA training set par aur fine-tune karo. Iske liye data ko SQuAD JSON format me convert karna padta hai, jahan har product ke liye paragraphs aur unke question-answer pairs hote hain. Ek epoch fine-tuning ke baad EM score chhe guna badh gaya aur F1-score dogune se zyada ho gaya. Aur agar seedha pretrained MiniLM ko sirf SubjQA par fine-tune karo (bina SQuAD ke), to result kaafi kharab milta hai — kyunki SubjQA me sirf 1,295 training examples hain aur overfitting ka risk hai. Lesson: bade general dataset par fine-tune karke phir chhote domain dataset par adapt karo.

Generative QA — RAG

Extractive QA ke aage hai generative (abstractive) QA, jahan model answer generate karta hai aur multiple passages se evidence synthesize kar sakta hai. State-of-the-art approach hai Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): retriever ke roop me DPR aur reader ki jagah ek generator (T5 ya BART jaisa seq2seq transformer). Dono ko end-to-end fine-tune kiya ja sakta hai. RAG-Sequence ek hi document se poora answer generate karta hai, jabki RAG-Token har token ke liye alag document use kar sakta hai — isliye RAG-Token aam taur par behtar hota hai. Book ke test me RAG ne sensible answers diye ("What is the main drawback?" par "the price", "no flash support"), lekin subjective questions par ye bhi confuse hua.

QA hierarchy of needs

Practical advice ye hai: pehle users ko useful search capabilities do, phir extractive component jodo, aur generative QA ko sirf tab explore karo jab pehle dono exhaust ho jayein. Reader ko creative tareekon se bhi use kiya ja sakta hai — jaise har product ke pros aur cons automatically extract karna, ya "What kind of camera?" jaise queries se zero-shot named entities nikaalna. Aage ki directions hain multimodal QA (text, tables aur images par) aur knowledge graphs par QA.

Yaad rakho: Retriever ki recall se system ki ceiling banti hai; reader ko EM aur F1 dono se measure karo; domain adaptation (SQuAD phir apna domain data) se sabse bada performance gain milta hai.

from haystack.pipeline import Pipeline
from haystack.eval import EvalDocuments

class EvalRetrieverPipeline:
    def __init__(self, retriever):
        self.retriever = retriever
        self.eval_retriever = EvalDocuments()
        pipe = Pipeline()
        pipe.add_node(component=self.retriever, name="ESRetriever", 
                      inputs=["Query"])
        pipe.add_node(component=self.eval_retriever, name="EvalRetriever", 
                      inputs=["ESRetriever"])
        self.pipeline = pipe

def evaluate_retriever(retriever, topk_values = [1,3,5,10,20]):
    topk_results = {}

    for topk in topk_values:
        # Create Pipeline
        p = EvalRetrieverPipeline(retriever)
        # Loop over each question-answers pair in test set
        run_pipeline(p, top_k_retriever=topk)
        # Get metrics
        topk_results[topk] = {"recall": p.eval_retriever.recall}
        
    return pd.DataFrame.from_dict(topk_results, orient="index")

from haystack.eval import EvalAnswers

def evaluate_reader(reader):
    score_keys = ['top_1_em', 'top_1_f1']
    eval_reader = EvalAnswers(skip_incorrect_retrieval=False)
    pipe = Pipeline()
    pipe.add_node(component=reader, name="QAReader", inputs=["Query"])
    pipe.add_node(component=eval_reader, name="EvalReader", inputs=["QAReader"])

    for l in labels_agg:
        doc = document_store.query(l.question, 
                                   filters={"question_id":[l.origin]})
        _ = pipe.run(query=l.question, documents=doc, labels=l)
                
    return {k:v for k,v in eval_reader.__dict__.items() if k in score_keys}

reader_eval = {}
reader_eval["Fine-tune on SQuAD"] = evaluate_reader(reader)

def create_paragraphs(df):
    paragraphs = []
    id2context = dict(zip(df["review_id"], df["context"]))
    for review_id, review in id2context.items():
        qas = []
        # Filter for all question-answer pairs about a specific context
        review_df = df.query(f"review_id == '{review_id}'")
        id2question = dict(zip(review_df["id"], review_df["question"]))
        # Build up the qas array
        for qid, question in id2question.items():
            # Filter for a single question ID
            question_df = df.query(f"id == '{qid}'").to_dict(orient="list")
            ans_start_idxs = question_df["answers.answer_start"][0].tolist()
            ans_text = question_df["answers.text"][0].tolist()
            # Fill answerable questions
            if len(ans_start_idxs):
                answers = [
                    {"text": text, "answer_start": answer_start}
                    for text, answer_start in zip(ans_text, ans_start_idxs)]
                is_impossible = False
            else:
                answers = []
                is_impossible = True
            # Add question-answer pairs to qas
            qas.append({"question": question, "id": qid, 
                        "is_impossible": is_impossible, "answers": answers})
        # Add context and question-answer pairs to paragraphs
        paragraphs.append({"qas": qas, "context": review})
    return paragraphs

import json

def convert_to_squad(dfs):
    for split, df in dfs.items():
        subjqa_data = {}
        # Create `paragraphs` for each product ID
        groups = (df.groupby("title").apply(create_paragraphs)
            .to_frame(name="paragraphs").reset_index())
        subjqa_data["data"] = groups.to_dict(orient="records")
        # Save the result to disk
        with open(f"electronics-{split}.json", "w+", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(subjqa_data, f)
            
convert_to_squad(dfs)

08Chapter 8 · Making Transformers Efficient in Production

Making Transformers Efficient in Production

Accuracy hi sab kuch nahi hai. Agar tumhara state-of-the-art model bahut slow ya bahut bada hai to wo production me bekaar hai. Is chapter me hum chaar techniques se transformers ko fast aur compact banate hain: knowledge distillation, quantization, pruning aur ONNX optimization. Case study hai intent detection — ek text-based assistant ka core component.

Intent detection kya hai

Intent detection me natural language text ko predefined actions ya intents me classify karna hota hai. Example: customer likhta hai "Hey, I'd like to rent a vehicle from Nov 1st to Nov 15th in Paris and I need a 15 passenger van" — to system ise Car Rental intent me daal kar sahi action trigger karta hai. Ek mushkil case hai out-of-scope queries — jab customer aisa sawaal poochhe jo kisi bhi predefined intent me na aata ho, to system ko fallback response dena chahiye, galat intent me daalna nahi.

Book me CLINC150 dataset use hua hai: 22,500 in-scope queries, 150 intents, 10 domains (banking, travel jaise), aur 1,200 out-of-scope queries jo ek alag oos class me hain. Baseline hai ek fine-tune hua BERT-base model jo lagbhag 94% accuracy deta hai.

Production ke teen constraints

  • Model performance: Test set par accuracy kitni hai — khaas taur par jab galti ki cost zyada ho ya millions examples par inference chalana ho.
  • Latency: Prediction kitni fast milti hai? Real-time environments me ye critical hai — jaise ek text assistant se baat-cheet karte waqt delay bardasht nahi hota.
  • Memory: Model disk aur RAM me kitni jagah leta hai? Billion-parameter models ko gigabytes chahiye hote hain — mobile ya edge devices par ye sabse badi problem hai.

Performance benchmark banana

Har technique ko compare karne ke liye book me ek PerformanceBenchmark class banayi gayi hai jo teen cheezein measure karti hai: accuracy (test set par), model size (state_dict ko torch.save() se disk par save karke MB me), aur latency (pipeline ko 10 baar warmup karke phir 100 runs par perf_counter() se average aur standard deviation). Baseline BERT ke numbers: size 418.16 MB, average latency 54.20 ms, accuracy 0.867. Latency hardware par depend karti hai — GPU par batch processing se behtar milti hai — isliye relative difference dekhna zyada important hai.

Ek real example se pata chalta hai ki ye techniques kitni powerful hain: ek engineering team ne knowledge distillation aur quantization combine karke apne BERT classifier ki latency aur throughput me 30 guna se zyada ka improvement paya. Aage ke sections me hum ek-ek karke ye techniques apply karte hain aur benchmark numbers se dekhte hain ki kya badla.

Yaad rakho: Production me accuracy ke saath latency aur memory bhi constraints hain. Pehle benchmark banao (accuracy, size, latency), phir har optimization ka asar usi benchmark se measure karo.

def compute_accuracy(self):
    """This overrides the PerformanceBenchmark.compute_accuracy() method"""
    preds, labels = [], []
    for example in self.dataset:
        pred = self.pipeline(example["text"])[0]["label"]
        label = example["intent"]
        preds.append(intents.str2int(pred))
        labels.append(label)
    accuracy = accuracy_score.compute(predictions=preds, references=labels)
    print(f"Accuracy on test set - {accuracy['accuracy']:.3f}")
    return accuracy

PerformanceBenchmark.compute_accuracy = compute_accuracy

import torch
from pathlib import Path

def compute_size(self):
    """This overrides the PerformanceBenchmark.compute_size() method"""
    state_dict = self.pipeline.model.state_dict()
    tmp_path = Path("model.pt")
    torch.save(state_dict, tmp_path)
    # Calculate size in megabytes
    size_mb = Path(tmp_path).stat().st_size / (1024 * 1024)
    # Delete temporary file
    tmp_path.unlink()
    print(f"Model size (MB) - {size_mb:.2f}")
    return {"size_mb": size_mb}

PerformanceBenchmark.compute_size = compute_size

import numpy as np

def time_pipeline(self, query="What is the pin number for my account?"):
    """This overrides the PerformanceBenchmark.time_pipeline() method"""
    latencies = []
    # Warmup
    for _ in range(10):
        _ = self.pipeline(query)
    # Timed run
    for _ in range(100):
        start_time = perf_counter()
        _ = self.pipeline(query)
        latency = perf_counter() - start_time
        latencies.append(latency)
    # Compute run statistics
    time_avg_ms = 1000 * np.mean(latencies)
    time_std_ms = 1000 * np.std(latencies)
    print(f"Average latency (ms) - {time_avg_ms:.2f} +\- {time_std_ms:.2f}")
    return {"time_avg_ms": time_avg_ms, "time_std_ms": time_std_ms}

PerformanceBenchmark.time_pipeline = time_pipeline

08.1Chapter 8 · Making Transformers Efficient in Production

Knowledge Distillation

Knowledge distillation ka idea simple hai: ek bada, slow lekin accurate teacher model apna knowledge ek chhote, fast student model ko transfer karta hai. Student teacher jaisa behave karna seekhta hai — sirf sahi labels se nahi, balki teacher ki soft probabilities se bhi.

Soft probabilities aur temperature

Teacher input par logits deta hai. Normal softmax se aksar ek class ki probability lagbhag 1 aur baaki ki lagbhag 0 ho jati hai — isse student ko labels ke alawa kuch naya nahi milta. Isliye logits ko temperature T se divide karke soften kiya jata hai: zyada T se distribution soft hoti hai aur pata chalta hai ki kaunsi classes ek doosre ke kareeb hain. Ye "dark knowledge" hai — wo information jo labels me nahi hoti. Jaise agar teacher car rental aur flight booking dono ko kuch probability deta hai, to student seekhta hai ki ye intents feature space me paas-paas hain.

Loss function

Student aur teacher ki softened distributions ke beech ka difference Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence se measure hota hai. Distillation loss hoti hai L_KD = T^2 × D_KL, jahan T^2 ek normalization factor hai kyunki soft labels se aane wale gradients ka magnitude 1/T^2 se scale hota hai. Student ka total loss hota hai L_student = α × L_CE + (1 − α) × L_KD, jahan L_CE ground truth labels par usual cross-entropy loss hai aur α dono losses ka relative weight control karta hai. Inference ke waqt temperature 1 par set karke standard softmax probabilities wapas mil jati hain.

Distillation pretraining me bhi

Distillation sirf fine-tuning me nahi, pretraining me bhi use hoti hai. Ek famous example me masked language modeling loss ke saath distillation loss aur ek cosine embedding loss joda gaya jo teacher aur student ke hidden state vectors ki direction ko align karta hai. Isse bana ek general-purpose student jo baad me downstream tasks par fine-tune ho sakta hai.

Book ka experiment — DistilBERT student

Teacher hai fine-tune hua BERT-base aur student hai DistilBERT (40% kam parameters). Rule of thumb ye hai ki distillation sabse achhi hoti hai jab teacher aur student same model type ke hon. Implementation ke liye TrainingArguments ko subclass karke α aur temperature add kiye gaye, aur Trainer ko subclass karke compute_loss() override kiya gaya — student aur teacher dono ke logits nikaalo, temperature se soften karo, KL divergence compute karo, aur weighted loss return karo. PyTorch ke nn.KLDivLoss() me inputs log probabilities me aur labels normal probabilities me chahiye hote hain.

Pehle α=1 (bina teacher signal ke) se DistilBERT ko fine-tune kiya: validation accuracy 92% mili, test accuracy 0.858, size 255.89 MB, latency 27.53 ms — matlab latency aadhi ho gayi sirf 1% accuracy khokar. Phir Optuna se hyperparameters search kiye gaye (20 trials): best values mile num_train_epochs 10, α 0.125, temperature 7. Matlab zyada tar training signal distillation term se aa raha tha. Final distilled model ki test accuracy 0.868 thi — teacher se bhi behtar — size wahi 255.89 MB aur latency 25.96 ms.

Yaad rakho: Teacher ki soft probabilities me dark knowledge hoti hai. Temperature distribution ko soften karta hai, KL divergence student ko teacher jaisa banata hai, aur α dono losses ko balance karta hai.

from transformers import TrainingArguments

class DistillationTrainingArguments(TrainingArguments):
    def __init__(self, *args, alpha=0.5, temperature=2.0, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.temperature = temperature
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/08_model-compression.ipynb)
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import Trainer

class DistillationTrainer(Trainer):
    def __init__(self, *args, teacher_model=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.teacher_model = teacher_model

    def compute_loss(self, model, inputs, return_outputs=False):
        device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
        inputs = inputs.to(device)
        outputs_stu = model(**inputs)
        # Extract cross-entropy loss and logits from student
        loss_ce = outputs_stu.loss
        logits_stu = outputs_stu.logits
        # Extract logits from teacher
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs_tea = self.teacher_model(**inputs)
            logits_tea = outputs_tea.logits
        # Soften probabilities and compute distillation loss
        loss_fct = nn.KLDivLoss(reduction="batchmean")
        loss_kd = self.args.temperature ** 2 * loss_fct(
            F.log_softmax(logits_stu / self.args.temperature, dim=-1),
            F.softmax(logits_tea / self.args.temperature, dim=-1))
        # Return weighted student loss
        loss = self.args.alpha * loss_ce + (1. - self.args.alpha) * loss_kd
        return (loss, outputs_stu) if return_outputs else loss

import pandas as pd

def plot_metrics(perf_metrics, current_optim_type):
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(perf_metrics, orient='index')

    for idx in df.index:
        df_opt = df.loc[idx]
        # Add a dashed circle around the current optimization type
        if idx == current_optim_type:
            plt.scatter(df_opt["time_avg_ms"], df_opt["accuracy"] * 100, 
                        alpha=0.5, s=df_opt["size_mb"], label=idx, 
                        marker='$\u25CC$')
        else:
            plt.scatter(df_opt["time_avg_ms"], df_opt["accuracy"] * 100, 
                        s=df_opt["size_mb"], label=idx, alpha=0.5)
            
    legend = plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1,1))
    for handle in (legend.legend_handles if hasattr(legend, "legend_handles") else legend.legendHandles):
        handle.set_sizes([20])

    plt.ylim(80,90)
    # Use the slowest model to define the x-axis range
    xlim = int(perf_metrics["BERT baseline"]["time_avg_ms"] + 3)
    plt.xlim(1, xlim)
    plt.ylabel("Accuracy (%)")
    plt.xlabel("Average latency (ms)")
    plt.show()

08.2Chapter 8 · Making Transformers Efficient in Production

Quantization aur Pruning

Distillation model ko chhota banata hai; quantization computations ko efficient banata hai. Weights aur activations ko 32-bit floating point (FP32) ki jagah 8-bit integer (INT8) me represent karo — model 4 guna tak chhota ho jata hai aur matrix multiplication bahut fast ho jati hai, aksar bina accuracy khoye.

Floating point vs fixed point

FP32 numbers sign, exponent aur significand se bante hain — exponent ki wajah se bahut badi range represent ho sakti hai. Training me ye precision chahiye hoti hai. Lekin inference me sirf forward pass chahiye, isliye kam precision kaafi hoti hai. Fixed-point format me real numbers ko B-bit integers ke roop me represent kiya jata hai, ek common scale factor se. Quantization me floating-point values f ki range [f_min, f_max] ko fixed-point range [q_min, q_max] me map kiya jata hai: f = S × (q − Z), jahan S scale factor hai aur Z zero point hai (jo f=0 ke barabar quantized value hai).

Transformers quantization ke liye perfect kyun hain

Transformer ke weights aur activations chhoti range me hote hain — book ke example me ek attention weight matrix ke values lagbhag [-0.1, 0.1] ke beech the. Isliye poori FP32 range ko squeeze nahi karna padta, sirf is chhoti range ko 256 INT8 values me map karna hota hai. Book ke timing test me FP32 matrix multiplication me 393 microseconds lage, jabki INT8 me sirf 23.3 microseconds — lagbhag 17 guna fast. Storage me bhi 4 guna ki bachat mili (ratio 3.9996). Dedicated backends (jaise x86 CPUs with AVX2 ya ARM CPUs) par aur bhi zyada gains milte hain.

Quantization ke teen tareeke

  • Dynamic quantization: Training me kuch nahi badalta; inference ke waqt weights pehle se INT8 me convert hote hain aur activations on-the-fly quantize hoti hain. Sabse simple tareeka, aur transformers ke liye currently best approach.
  • Static quantization: Activations ka quantization scheme pehle se ek representative data sample par observe karke calculate kiya jata hai, taaki inference me FP32-INT8 conversion na karna pade. Iske liye achha data sample chahiye aur ek extra step lagta hai.
  • Quantization-aware training: Training ke dauraan hi FP32 values ko "fake" quantize karke quantization ka effect simulate kiya jata hai — forward aur backward dono passes me. Isse accuracy sabse achhi rehti hai, lekin sabse zyada mehnat lagti hai.

PyTorch me dynamic quantization ek line me hoti hai: quantize_dynamic(model, {nn.Linear}, dtype=torch.qint8) — sirf linear layers quantize hote hain. Book ke distilled model par iske results: size 132.40 MB (aadha), latency 12.54 ms, accuracy 0.876 — size aur speed dono behtar, aur accuracy me halki badhotri bhi.

Weight pruning — weights ko hatana

Quantization precision kam karta hai; pruning weights ko poori tarah hata deta hai. Idea ye hai ki importance scores compute karke top k percent weights rakho aur baaki ko zero kar do — model sparse ban jata hai aur sparse matrix format me compactly store ho sakta hai. Magnitude pruning me score weight ka magnitude hota hai, aur ise iterative tareeke se apply kiya jata hai: train karo, kam important weights hatao, dobara train karo. Ek cubic sparsity scheduler se pruning rate shuru me tez aur baad me dheere rakhi jati hai. Problem ye hai ki magnitude pruning transfer learning me un connections ko hata sakta hai jo pretraining me important the.

Movement pruning ek adaptive approach hai: scores weights se derive nahi hote, balki fine-tuning ke dauraan gradient descent se seekhe jate hain. Intuition ye hai ki jo weights zero se sabse zyada "move" kar rahe hain, wo sabse important hain. Lekin ek badi limitation hai: aaj ka hardware sparse matrix operations ke liye optimize nahi hai, isliye pruning se storage to kam hota hai lekin latency me utna faida nahi milta.

Yaad rakho: Quantization precision kam karke speed aur memory dono bachata hai (INT8, dynamic sabse simple); pruning weights hatakar sparsity badhata hai, lekin hardware support abhi limited hai.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def _sparsity(t, t_0=0, dt=1, s_i=0, s_f=0.9, N=100):
    return s_f + (s_i - s_f) * (1 - (t - t_0) / (N * dt))**3

steps = np.linspace(0,100,100)
values = [_sparsity(t) for t in steps]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(steps, values)
ax.set_ylim(0,1)
ax.set_xlim(0,100)
ax.set_xlabel("Pruning step")
ax.set_ylabel("Sparsity")
plt.grid(linestyle="dashed")
plt.show()

08.3Chapter 8 · Making Transformers Efficient in Production

ONNX aur Optimized Inference

Aakhri technique hai graph optimization — model ko ONNX format me export karke ONNX Runtime (ORT) se chalana. Isse bina accuracy khoye latency aur kam ho jati hai, aur quantization ke saath combine karne par sabse bada overall gain milta hai.

ONNX kya hai

ONNX ek open standard hai jo deep learning models ke liye common operators aur common file format define karta hai. Jab model ONNX me export hota hai, to uske operators se ek computational graph (intermediate representation) banta hai — har node ek input leta hai, ek operation (jaise Add ya Squeeze) apply karta hai, aur output agle nodes ko deta hai. Isse frameworks ke beech switch karna aasan ho jata hai: PyTorch me train kiya model ONNX me export karke TensorFlow me import ho sakta hai, aur vice versa.

ONNX Runtime se optimization

ORT ka asli faida hai graph optimization: operator fusion aur constant folding. Operator fusion me ek operator (aksar activation function) ko doosre me merge kar diya jata hai taaki dono ek hi step me execute hon — jaise matrix product ka result pehle memory me likhna aur phir activation compute karna, iski jagah dono ek saath ho jate hain. Constant folding me constant expressions ko runtime ki jagah compile time par evaluate kar liya jata hai. ORT execution providers ka interface bhi deta hai, jisse model alag hardware (CPU, GPU) par chal sakta hai.

Model convert karna aur chalana

Transformers library me convert_graph_to_onnx.convert() function hai jo model ko pipeline me wrap karke, placeholder inputs se graph record karke, dynamic axes define karke aur graph ko save karke conversion karta hai. Phir InferenceSession banaya jata hai — graph optimization level ORT_ENABLE_ALL ke saath — aur run() se logits milte hain. Book me ONNX model ne test example par sahi label (61) predict kiya. Kyunki ONNX model text-classification pipeline ke saath compatible nahi hai, book me ek chhoti OnnxPipeline class banayi gayi hai jo tokenize karke, numpy arrays me convert karke, session run karke aur softmax lagakar label aur score return karti hai.

Benchmark results — sab kuch combine karke

Distilled model ko ONNX + ORT me convert karne par latency 25.96 ms se 21.02 ms ho gayi, size 255.88 MB aur accuracy 0.868 — bina accuracy khoye speed gain. Phir ORT ki dynamic quantization (quantize_dynamic with QuantType.QInt8) lagane par size 64.20 MB aur latency 9.24 ms ho gayi, accuracy 0.877. Ye PyTorch quantization se lagbhag 30% behtar hai, kyunki ORT embedding layer ko bhi quantize karta hai jabki PyTorch sirf linear layers ko karta hai.

Poora safar dekho: BERT baseline (418.16 MB, 54.20 ms, 0.867) se shuru karke distillation + ORT quantization tak (64.20 MB, 9.24 ms, 0.877) — model lagbhag 6.5 guna chhota, lagbhag 6 guna fast, aur accuracy thodi behtar bhi. Conclusion: quantization aur ORT conversion se minimal effort me sabse bade gains milte hain. Ye techniques sirf intent detection tak limited nahi hain — inhe question answering, NER ya language modeling par bhi apply kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: ONNX model ko framework-independent graph banata hai; ORT operator fusion aur constant folding se optimize karta hai; distillation + ORT quantization ka combination sabse bada gain deta hai.

from onnxruntime import (GraphOptimizationLevel, InferenceSession, 
                         SessionOptions)

def create_model_for_provider(model_path, provider="CPUExecutionProvider"): 
    options = SessionOptions()
    options.intra_op_num_threads = 1
    options.graph_optimization_level = GraphOptimizationLevel.ORT_ENABLE_ALL
    session = InferenceSession(str(model_path), options, providers=[provider])
    session.disable_fallback()
    return session

Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/08_model-compression.ipynb)
from scipy.special import softmax

class OnnxPipeline:
    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer):
        self.model = model
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        
    def __call__(self, query):
        model_inputs = self.tokenizer(query, return_tensors="pt")
        inputs_onnx = {k: v.cpu().detach().numpy() 
                       for k, v in model_inputs.items()}
        logits = self.model.run(None, inputs_onnx)[0][0, :]
        probs = softmax(logits)
        pred_idx = np.argmax(probs).item()
        return [{"label": intents.int2str(pred_idx), "score": probs[pred_idx]}]
Python — notebook code (GitHub: https://github.com/nlp-with-transformers/notebooks/blob/main/08_model-compression.ipynb)

pipe(query)
